@code {
    /// <summary>
    /// How many events the list will draw. §11.4's rule is that administration sees everything and
    /// narrows "only on explicit request", so this is a rendering bound rather than a filter: when it is
    /// reached the page says so and points at the filter, instead of quietly answering a smaller
    /// question. Larger than the hidden-records cap because these three logs are the busiest tables in
    /// the database and a day's worth of one service can pass a hundred rows before lunch.
    /// </summary>
    private const int ListCap = 200;

    private EventExplorerQuery _query = default!;
    private IReadOnlyList<ExplorerEvent>? _events;

    [CascadingParameter]
    private HttpContext HttpContext { get; set; } = default!;

    [SupplyParameterFromQuery(Name = EventExplorerQuery.StreamField)]
    private string[]? Streams { get; set; }

    [SupplyParameterFromQuery(Name = EventExplorerQuery.SubjectField)]
    private string? Subject { get; set; }

    [SupplyParameterFromQuery(Name = EventExplorerQuery.ActorField)]
    private string? Actor { get; set; }

    [SupplyParameterFromQuery(Name = EventExplorerQuery.TypeField)]
    private string? EventTypeChoice { get; set; }

    [SupplyParameterFromQuery(Name = EventExplorerQuery.FromField)]
    private string? From { get; set; }

    [SupplyParameterFromQuery(Name = EventExplorerQuery.ToField)]
    private string? To { get; set; }

    protected override async Task OnInitializedAsync()
    {
        _query = EventExplorerQuery.Parse(
            Streams, Subject, Actor, EventTypeChoice, From, To, RestaurantClock);

        _events = await Explorer.ListAsync(_query.Filter, ListCap, HttpContext.RequestAborted);
    }

    /// <summary>
    /// The line above the list. It says whether the count is the whole truth: at <see cref="ListCap"/>
    /// there may be more, and §11.4 means the page has to admit that rather than let a round number look
    /// like an answer.
    /// </summary>
    private string CountSentence(int count)
    {
        string noun = count == 1 ? "event" : "events";
        string scope = _query.IsNarrowed ? "matching the filter" : "in total";

        return count == ListCap
            ? $"{count} {noun} {scope} — capped at {ListCap}; narrow the filter to see past it."
            : $"{count} {noun} {scope}.";
    }

    /// <summary>The badge link: this same view, restricted to the row's own stream.</summary>
    private string OnlyThisStreamPath(ExplorerEvent entry) => _query.PathWithStreams(
        entry.Stream == EventStream.Security,
        entry.Stream == EventStream.Order,
        entry.Stream == EventStream.Menu);

    /// <summary>
    /// Where the row's subject lives. Security and menu events name their subject directly; an order
    /// event's subject is one guest's order, and the screen that renders an order in full is its
    /// sitting's (§11.4), so that is where it points. A stream this build does not know about gets no
    /// link rather than a guessed one.
    /// </summary>
    private static string? SubjectPath(ExplorerEvent entry) => entry.Stream switch
    {
        EventStream.Security => $"/administration/people/{entry.SubjectIdentifier}",
        EventStream.Menu => $"/administration/menu/{entry.SubjectIdentifier}",
        EventStream.Order => entry.ContextIdentifier is { } sittingIdentifier
            ? $"/administration/sittings/{sittingIdentifier}"
            : null,
        _ => null,
    };

    private static string StreamLabel(string stream) => stream switch
    {
        EventStream.Security => "Security",
        EventStream.Order => "Order",
        EventStream.Menu => "Menu",
        _ => stream,
    };

    /// <summary>
    /// A friendly label for the row, chosen by stream. Every branch falls back to the stored string, and
    /// so does the stream switch itself: §11.4 requires this screen to render what is actually in the
    /// tables, and a word this build has not caught up with must appear as itself rather than as a lie or
    /// a crash. The same rule, and mostly the same words, as ManageSitting's and HiddenRecords'.
    /// </summary>
    private static string DescribeEvent(ExplorerEvent entry) => entry.Stream switch
    {
        EventStream.Security => DescribeSecurityEventType(entry.EventType),
        EventStream.Order => DescribeOrderEventType(entry.EventType),
        EventStream.Menu => DescribeMenuEventType(entry.EventType),
        _ => entry.EventType,
    };

    /// <summary>
    /// The nineteen <c>security_event.event_type</c> values §8.2's CHECK admits (§3.4–§3.7). "TOTP" is
    /// spelled "authenticator" here for the same reason the enrollment pages spell it that way: the
    /// person reading this screen manages a restaurant, and the acronym is a protocol name.
    /// </summary>
    private static string DescribeSecurityEventType(string eventType) => eventType switch
    {
        "account_created" => "Account created",
        "account_deactivated" => "Account deactivated",
        "account_reactivated" => "Account reactivated",
        "password_changed" => "Password changed",
        "password_reset_by_administrator" => "Password reset by an administrator",
        "forced_password_change_completed" => "Forced password change completed",
        "totp_enrolled" => "Authenticator enrolled",
        "totp_removed" => "Authenticator removed",
        "totp_cleared_by_administrator" => "Authenticator cleared by an administrator",
        "forced_totp_enrollment_completed" => "Forced authenticator enrollment completed",
        "recovery_code_used" => "Recovery code used",
        "recovery_codes_regenerated" => "Recovery codes regenerated",
        "passkey_registered" => "Passkey registered",
        "passkey_removed" => "Passkey removed",
        "role_granted" => "Role granted",
        "role_revoked" => "Role revoked",
        "sign_in_succeeded" => "Signed in",
        "sign_in_failed" => "Sign-in failed",
        "account_locked_out" => "Account locked out",
        _ => eventType,
    };

    /// <summary>The five <c>order_event.event_type</c> values, in HiddenRecords' words.</summary>
    private static string DescribeOrderEventType(string eventType) => eventType switch
    {
        "guest_submission" => "Guest send",
        "staff_edit" => "Staff edit",
        "price_adjustment" => "Price change",
        "fulfillment" => "Delivered",
        "fulfillment_reversal" => "Delivery undone",
        _ => eventType,
    };

    /// <summary>The five <c>menu_item_event.event_type</c> values (§7, §8.2).</summary>
    private static string DescribeMenuEventType(string eventType) => eventType switch
    {
        "created" => "Item created",
        "name_changed" => "Renamed",
        "price_changed" => "Repriced",
        "activated" => "Back on the menu",
        "deactivated" => "Off the menu (86'd)",
        _ => eventType,
    };

    /// <summary>
    /// The four <c>order_event.actor_role</c> values. <c>guest</c> is a capacity rather than a stored
    /// role (§0, §3.7) — an administrator eating lunch appears here as a guest, and that is correct.
    /// </summary>
    private static string DescribeActorRole(string actorRole) => actorRole switch
    {
        "guest" => "a guest",
        "kitchen" => "the kitchen",
        "counter" => "the counter",
        "administrator" => "an administrator",
        _ => actorRole,
    };

    private string Money(decimal amount) => MoneyText.Format(amount, Options.CurrencyCode);
}

@page "/administration/hidden-records"
@attribute [ExcludeFromInteractiveRouting]
@attribute [Authorize(Policy = AuthorizationPolicies.Administration)]
@using System.Globalization
@using MyRestaurant.DataAccess.Orders
@using MyRestaurant.DataAccess.Sittings

@* The hidden-records view (TECHNICAL_SPECIFICATION §6.8, §11.4).

   §6.8's second half, verbatim: "Administrators locate hidden orders in the **hidden-records view**
   (§11.4): every currently-hidden order system-wide, filterable by username, date range, and table, each
   row expandable to the complete stored record — full event log, visibility log, sitting context,
   unprojected — with a per-record Unhide (appends `unhidden_by_administrator`)."

   This is the only unhide path in the system. §6.8 gives the hide to the owner and says plainly that
   there is no user-facing undo, so a guest who hides the wrong meal has exactly one recourse: ask a
   manager, who arrives here.

   Static SSR, like every administration surface. The filter is a plain GET form — a filter is a
   bookmarkable question, not a mutation, so it belongs in the URL rather than in component state, and a
   GET form needs no antiforgery token and no handler. The Unhide is a POST that redirects back to the
   same filtered URL (post/redirect/get), so a refresh cannot re-append.

   **Expansion is one row at a time, by URL.** §11.4 requires the complete record — "never projected or
   truncated" — and a complete record is three queries per order. Rendering fifty of them to draw a list
   would be two hundred round trips for a page somebody is skimming. ?record={order} is the "expandable"
   in §6.8: the list is always complete, and the record of the row an administrator actually opened is
   fetched in full. That is narrowing on explicit request in the direction §11.4 asks for. *@

        @foreach (HiddenOrderSummary summary in _hidden)

                            <code>guest_order.table_sitting_identifier</code> is a NOT NULL foreign key —

                    }
                    else

                        <dl class="hidden-facts">
                            <div>

                            </div>
                            <div>
                                <dt>Settled</dt>
                                <dd>
                                    @if (_sitting.ClosedAt is { } sittingClosedAt)
                                    {
                                        @RestaurantClock.DateAndTime(sittingClosedAt)
                                        @if (!string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(_sitting.ClosedByName))
                                        {
                                            <text> by @_sitting.ClosedByName</text>
                                        }
                                    }
                                    else
                                    {
                                        <text>still open</text>
                                    }
                                </dd>
                            </div>
                            <div>
                                <dt>At the table</dt>
                                <dd>
                                    @_sitting.MemberCount
                                    @(_sitting.MemberCount == 1 ? "person" : "people") ·
                                    @_sitting.OrderCount @(_sitting.OrderCount == 1 ? "order" : "orders")
                                </dd>
                            </div>
                            <div>
                                <dt>Settled total</dt>
                                <dd>
                                    @Money(_sitting.SettledTotalAmount ?? _sitting.CurrentTotalAmount)
                                    @if (_sitting.HasPostCloseCorrections)
                                    {
                                        @* §5.3: the stamped total is never rewritten, so when §6.7
                                           corrections exist both numbers are shown. *@
                                        <span class="hidden-corrected">
                                            corrected to @Money(_sitting.CurrentTotalAmount)
                                        </span>
                                    }
                                </dd>
                            </div>
                        </dl>
                    }

                    @* ---- visibility log (§6.8) -------------------------------------------------- *@
                    <h3 class="hidden-heading">Visibility log</h3>

                    @if (_visibilityLog.Count == 0)
                    {
                        <p class="hidden-muted">
                            No visibility events, which contradicts this order appearing on this page at
                            all — worth reporting.
                        </p>
                    }
                    else
                    {
                        <ol class="hidden-events">
                            @foreach (OrderVisibilityEntry visibilityEvent in _visibilityLog)
                            {
                                <li>
                                    <span class="hidden-event-type">
                                        @DescribeVisibilityEvent(visibilityEvent.EventType)
                                    </span>
                                    <span class="hidden-muted-inline">
                                        @visibilityEvent.ActorName ·
                                        @RestaurantClock.DateAndTimeWithSeconds(visibilityEvent.OccurredAt)
                                    </span>
                                </li>
                            }
                        </ol>
                    }

                    @* ---- the complete stored record (§11.4) ------------------------------------- *@
                    <h3 class="hidden-heading">The record</h3>

                    @if (_record is null)
                    {
                        <p class="hidden-muted">
                            That order no longer exists. The row above came from a list read moments ago,
                            so this means it has been removed between the two reads — worth reporting,
                            because nothing in this system deletes an order.
                        </p>
                    }
                    else if (_record.Events.Count == 0)
                    {
                        <p class="hidden-muted">
                            The order row exists with no events on it. Only reachable if a write created it
                            and then rolled back its event, which the transaction does not do — worth
                            reporting if you are seeing it.
                        </p>
                    }
                    else
                    {
                        <p class="hidden-muted">
                            Every event on this order, oldest first and complete —
                            @_record.Events.Count @(_record.Events.Count == 1 ? "event" : "events").
                            Removed lines, undone deliveries, and superseded prices are all still here,
                            because the history outliving the state is the point of the log (ADR-0002).
                        </p>

                        <ol class="hidden-events">
                            @foreach (StoredOrderEvent stored in _record.Events)
                            {
                                <li>
                                    <div class="hidden-event-head">
                                        <span class="hidden-event-sequence">#@stored.SequenceNumber</span>
                                        <span class="hidden-event-type">
                                            @DescribeEventType(stored.EventType)
                                        </span>
                                        <span class="hidden-muted-inline">
                                            @stored.ActorName as @DescribeActorRole(stored.ActorRole) ·
                                            @RestaurantClock.DateAndTimeWithSeconds(stored.OccurredAt)
                                        </span>
                                    </div>

                                    @if (stored.Operations.Count == 0)
                                    {
                                        <p class="hidden-muted">
                                            No operations recorded, which §6.5.1 forbids — worth reporting.
                                        </p>
                                    }
                                    else
                                    {
                                        <ul class="hidden-operations">
                                            @foreach (StoredOrderOperation operation in stored.Operations)
                                            {
                                                <li>@DescribeOperation(operation)</li>
                                            }
                                        </ul>
                                    }
                                </li>
                            }
                        </ol>
                    }

                    @* ---- unhide (§6.8) --------------------------------------------------------- *@
                    <div class="hidden-unhide">
                        <p>
                            <strong>Put this back on @summary.OwnerName's history?</strong>
                            An <code>unhidden</code> row is appended with your name and the time; the
                            <code>hidden</code> row stays where it is, so the log will show that it was
                            hidden and then restored rather than pretending neither happened.
                        </p>

                        <form method="post" @formname="unhide-order" @onsubmit="UnhideAsync">
                            <AntiforgeryToken />
                            <input type="hidden" name="@OrderField" value="@summary.GuestOrderIdentifier" />

                            <div class="form-actions">
                                <button type="submit" class="button-primary">Unhide this record</button>
                                <a class="button-secondary" href="@ListPath()">Leave it hidden</a>
                            </div>
                        </form>
                    </div>
                }
            </article>
        }
    }

    <p><a href="/administration">Back to people</a></p>
</section>

   the static wwwroot/app.css rather than the component-scoped bundle, so component CSS isolation is not
   active here; these live inline to avoid editing the shared stylesheet for one screen. *@

@code {
    /// <summary>
    /// How many hidden orders the list will draw. §11.4's rule is that administration sees everything and
    /// narrows "only on explicit request", so this is a rendering bound rather than a filter: when it is
    /// reached the page says so and points at the filter, instead of silently answering a smaller
    /// question.
    /// </summary>
    private const int ListCap = 100;

    /// <summary>What an <c>&lt;input type="date"&gt;</c> submits, and the only format read back.</summary>
    private const string DatePattern = "yyyy-MM-dd";

    /// <summary>The one field the POST handler reads; the order travels in a hidden input.</summary>
    private const string OrderField = "order";

    private IReadOnlyList<RestaurantTableSummary> _tables = [];
    private IReadOnlyList<HiddenOrderSummary>? _hidden;
    private HiddenOrderFilter _filter = HiddenOrderFilter.Everything;

    // Only populated for the one row ?record= names.
    private SittingOrderRecord? _record;
    private CounterSittingSummary? _sitting;
    private IReadOnlyList<OrderVisibilityEntry> _visibilityLog = [];

    private string? _flashMessage;
    private string? _errorMessage;
    private string? _dateProblem;

    [CascadingParameter]
    private HttpContext HttpContext { get; set; } = default!;

    [SupplyParameterFromQuery]
    private string? Username { get; set; }

    [SupplyParameterFromQuery]
    private string? From { get; set; }

    [SupplyParameterFromQuery]
    private string? To { get; set; }

    [SupplyParameterFromQuery]
    private Guid? Table { get; set; }

    [SupplyParameterFromQuery]
    private Guid? Record { get; set; }

    [SupplyParameterFromQuery]
    private string? Done { get; set; }

    protected override async Task OnInitializedAsync()
    {
        await LoadAsync();

        if (HttpMethods.IsGet(HttpContext.Request.Method))
        {
            _flashMessage = FlashFor(Done);
        }
    }

    private async Task LoadAsync()
    {
        CancellationToken cancellationToken = HttpContext.RequestAborted;

        _tables = await Tables.ListTablesAsync(cancellationToken);
        _filter = BuildFilter();
        _hidden = await History.ListHiddenOrdersAsync(_filter, ListCap, cancellationToken);

        _record = null;
        _sitting = null;
        _visibilityLog = [];

        if (Record is not { } guestOrderIdentifier)
        {
            return;
        }

        // Only expand a row that is actually in the list. A ?record= naming an order that is not hidden —
        // or not there at all — would otherwise render a full record with an Unhide button under a list
        // that does not contain it, which reads as though the list were wrong.
        HiddenOrderSummary? summary = _hidden
            .FirstOrDefault(candidate => candidate.GuestOrderIdentifier == guestOrderIdentifier);

        if (summary is null)
        {
            _errorMessage =
                "That record is not in the list below — it may have been unhidden already, or the filter " +
                "may exclude it. Clear the filter to look again.";
            return;
        }

        _record = await SittingRecords.GetOrderRecordAsync(guestOrderIdentifier, cancellationToken);
        _visibilityLog = await History.ListVisibilityLogAsync(guestOrderIdentifier, cancellationToken);
        _sitting = await CounterReads.GetSittingAsync(summary.SittingIdentifier, cancellationToken);
    }

    /// <summary>
    /// §6.8's three filters, from the query string. The dates are read in the restaurant's own zone
    /// through <see cref="RestaurantTime"/> (§8.1): an administrator typing 26 July means the
    /// restaurant's 26 July, and the range is half-open — the start of that day to the start of the day
    /// after the upper bound — so the last microsecond of an evening cannot fall outside it.
    /// </summary>
    private HiddenOrderFilter BuildFilter()
    {
        DateOnly? from = ParseDate(From, "the earlier date");
        DateOnly? to = ParseDate(To, "the later date");

        if (from is { } lower && to is { } upper && upper < lower)
        {
            _dateProblem =
                "The later date is before the earlier one, so the range was ignored. Swap them, or clear " +
                "one of the two.";
            from = null;
            to = null;
        }

        return new HiddenOrderFilter(
            Username,
            from is { } start ? RestaurantClock.StartOfDay(start) : null,
            to is { } end ? RestaurantClock.StartOfNextDay(end) : null,
            Table);
    }

    private DateOnly? ParseDate(string? value, string which)
    {
        if (string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(value))
        {
            return null;
        }

        if (DateOnly.TryParseExact(
                value.Trim(), DatePattern, CultureInfo.InvariantCulture, DateTimeStyles.None,
                out DateOnly parsed))
        {
            return parsed;
        }

        // Only reachable from a hand-edited URL: the date input submits yyyy-MM-dd or nothing at all.
        _dateProblem = $"Could not read {which}, so it was ignored. Dates are year-month-day.";
        return null;
    }

    /// <summary>
    /// §6.8's per-record Unhide, through the workflow so the change is announced (§9) and the owner's
    /// history page stops omitting it. The service re-checks under its own lock that the order is still
    /// hidden, so two administrators pressing this at once produce one <c>unhidden</c> row and one honest
    /// "somebody got there first".
    /// </summary>
    private async Task UnhideAsync()
    {
        if (PersonPrincipal.IdentifierFor(HttpContext.User) is not { } administrator)
        {
            // Endpoint authorization already guarantees an administrator; this is the belt to that brace,
            // because order_visibility_event.actor_person_identifier is NOT NULL and has no anonymous
            // option.
            _errorMessage = "Your session could not be identified. Sign in again and retry.";
            await LoadAsync();
            return;
        }

        IFormCollection form = await HttpContext.Request.ReadFormAsync(HttpContext.RequestAborted);

        // Not a second read of the body: the Blazor endpoint has already parsed the form to find this
        // handler, and HttpRequest caches the parsed collection. Same shape as AdministrationSittings.
        string? postedOrder = form[OrderField];

        if (!Guid.TryParse(postedOrder, out Guid guestOrderIdentifier))
        {
            _errorMessage = "That request did not name a record, so nothing was unhidden.";
            await LoadAsync();
            return;
        }

        UnhideOrderResult result = await Visibility.UnhideAsync(
            guestOrderIdentifier, administrator, HttpContext.RequestAborted);

        if (result.Outcome is UnhideOrderOutcome.Unhidden or UnhideOrderOutcome.NotHidden)
        {
            // Post/redirect/get, back to the same filtered list minus the expanded row — the record is no
            // longer hidden, so it is no longer on this page, and leaving ?record= on the URL would only
            // produce the "not in the list" message. NotHidden redirects too: another administrator got
            // there first, which is the system working.
            Navigation.NavigateTo(ListPath(
                result.Outcome is UnhideOrderOutcome.Unhidden ? "unhidden" : "already-visible"));
            return;
        }

        _errorMessage =
            "That order no longer exists, so there was nothing to unhide. Reload the page to see the " +
            "current list.";
        await LoadAsync();
    }

    /// <summary>
    /// The list URL with the current filter preserved and, optionally, an outcome word. Rebuilt rather
    /// than reusing the incoming query string so <c>?record=</c> is dropped and nothing else is.
    /// </summary>
    /// <summary>Whether this row is the one <c>?record=</c> named and the record was actually loaded for.</summary>
    private bool IsExpanded(HiddenOrderSummary summary)
        => Record == summary.GuestOrderIdentifier;

    /// <summary>
    /// The line above the list. It says whether the count is the whole truth: at <see cref="ListCap"/>
    /// there may be more, and §11.4 means the page has to admit that rather than let a round number look
    /// like an answer.
    /// </summary>
    private string CountSentence(int count)
    {
        string noun = count == 1 ? "hidden order" : "hidden orders";
        string scope = _filter.IsNarrowed ? "matching the filter" : "in total";

        return count == ListCap
            ? $"{count} {noun} {scope} — capped at {ListCap}; narrow the filter to see past it."
            : $"{count} {noun} {scope}.";
    }

    private string ListPath(string? done = null)
    {
        List<string> parts = [];

        if (!string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(Username))
        {
            parts.Add($"username={Uri.EscapeDataString(Username.Trim())}");
        }

        if (!string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(From))
        {
            parts.Add($"from={Uri.EscapeDataString(From.Trim())}");
        }

        if (!string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(To))
        {
            parts.Add($"to={Uri.EscapeDataString(To.Trim())}");
        }

        if (Table is { } tableIdentifier)
        {
            parts.Add($"table={tableIdentifier}");
        }

        if (done is not null)
        {
            parts.Add($"done={done}");
        }

        return parts.Count == 0
            ? "/administration/hidden-records"
            : $"/administration/hidden-records?{string.Join("&", parts)}";
    }

    private string RecordPath(HiddenOrderSummary summary)
    {
        string list = ListPath();
        string separator = list.Contains('?', StringComparison.Ordinal) ? "&" : "?";

        return $"{list}{separator}record={summary.GuestOrderIdentifier}";
    }

    private static string SittingPath(HiddenOrderSummary summary)
        => $"/administration/sittings/{summary.SittingIdentifier}";

    private static string? FlashFor(string? done) => done switch
    {
        "unhidden" =>
            "Unhidden. It is back on its owner's history page, and the visibility log records that you " +
            "put it there.",
        "already-visible" =>
            "It was not hidden any more — another administrator had already unhidden it, so nothing was " +
            "appended.",
        _ => null,
    };

    /// <summary>
    /// The two <c>order_visibility_event.event_type</c> values §8.2's CHECK admits, falling back to the
    /// stored string. §6.8's prose calls the administrator's row "unhidden_by_administrator"; the stored
    /// word is <c>unhidden</c>, and there is no guest unhide to distinguish it from, so who did it is the
    /// actor beside it rather than a second word.
    /// </summary>
    private static string DescribeVisibilityEvent(string eventType) => eventType switch
    {
        "hidden" => "Hidden by the owner",
        "unhidden" => "Restored by an administrator",
        _ => eventType,
    };

    /// <summary>
    /// A friendly label for the five <c>order_event.event_type</c> values §8.2's CHECK admits, falling
    /// back to the stored string for anything else. The words are spelled out here rather than taken from
    /// <c>OrderEventVocabulary</c>, which is internal to the data-access assembly on purpose — a display
    /// label is not the writer's business, and a reader that threw on an unrecognised word would blank the
    /// one page whose job is to show what is actually stored. Same shape as ManageSitting's.
    /// </summary>
    private static string DescribeEventType(string eventType) => eventType switch
    {
        "guest_submission" => "Guest send",
        "staff_edit" => "Staff edit",
        "price_adjustment" => "Price change",
        "fulfillment" => "Delivered",
        "fulfillment_reversal" => "Delivery undone",
        _ => eventType,
    };

    /// <summary>
    /// The four <c>order_event.actor_role</c> values, on the same terms. <c>guest</c> is a capacity rather
    /// than a stored role (§0, §3.7) — an administrator eating lunch appears here as a guest, and that is
    /// correct.
    /// </summary>
    private static string DescribeActorRole(string actorRole) => actorRole switch
    {
        "guest" => "a guest",
        "kitchen" => "the kitchen",
        "counter" => "the counter",
        "administrator" => "an administrator",
        _ => actorRole,
    };

    /// <summary>
    /// One stored operation in a sentence. The five kinds are the discriminators the reader's UNION
    /// projects; an unknown one renders as itself beside the line it names, so nothing is ever swallowed.
    /// </summary>
    private string DescribeOperation(StoredOrderOperation operation) => operation.OperationKind switch
    {
        "line_added" =>
            $"Added {operation.Quantity} × {operation.MenuItemName} at " +
            $"{Money(operation.UnitPriceAmount ?? 0m)} each{NoteSuffix(operation.CustomizationNote)}",
        "line_removed" =>
            $"Removed {operation.Quantity} × {operation.MenuItemName}{ReasonSuffix(operation.Reason)}",
        "line_price_adjusted" =>
            $"{operation.Quantity} × {operation.MenuItemName} repriced to " +
            $"{Money(operation.NewUnitPriceAmount ?? 0m)} each{ReasonSuffix(operation.Reason)}",
        "line_fulfilled" =>
            $"{operation.Quantity} × {operation.MenuItemName} delivered",
        "line_fulfillment_reverted" =>
            $"{operation.Quantity} × {operation.MenuItemName} put back with the kitchen",
        _ => $"{operation.OperationKind} on {operation.Quantity} × {operation.MenuItemName}",
    };

    private static string NoteSuffix(string? note)
        => string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(note) ? string.Empty : $" — “{note.Trim()}”";

    private static string ReasonSuffix(string? reason)
        => string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(reason) ? string.Empty : $" — {reason.Trim()}";

    private string Money(decimal amount) => MoneyText.Format(amount, Options.CurrencyCode);
}

@page "/administration/menu/{MenuItemId:guid}"
@attribute [ExcludeFromInteractiveRouting]
@attribute [Authorize(Policy = AuthorizationPolicies.Administration)]
@using MyRestaurant.DataAccess.Menu
@using MyRestaurant.WebApplication.Menu
@using MyRestaurant.WebApplication.Orders
@inject IMenuDirectory MenuItems
@inject IMenuEventLog MenuEvents
@inject IMenuWorkflow MenuChanges
@inject RestaurantOptions Options
@inject NavigationManager Navigation
@inject RestaurantTime RestaurantClock

@* Manage one menu item (TECHNICAL_SPECIFICATION §7, §11.4). Administrator only (endpoint
   authorization). Static SSR: rename, reprice, and the availability toggle are full-page form posts.
   Successful changes redirect back here (post/redirect/get) carrying a one-word outcome so a refresh does
   not re-post; the shape ManageTable established.

   Rename and reprice are two forms rather than one "save", because §7's event vocabulary has
   `name_changed` and `price_changed` as separate types with mutually exclusive payload columns — a
   combined save would write two events anyway and would then have to decide what to do when one half
   changed nothing.

   The history below is complete and uncapped, oldest first. §11.4: administration renders "the complete
   stored record everywhere — full event streams … never projected or truncated for the administrator". A
   price argument is settled by reading forward from `created`, so that is the direction it renders. *@

<PageTitle>@(_item is null ? "Manage menu item" : $"Manage {_item.Name}")</PageTitle>

@if (_item is null)
{
    <section class="panel account-panel">
        <p class="eyebrow">Administration</p>
        <h1>Menu item not found</h1>
        <p class="lede">No menu item exists with that identifier. It may have never existed, or the link is stale.</p>

    </section>
}
else
{
    <section class="panel account-panel">
        <p class="eyebrow">Administration — menu</p>
        <h1>@_item.Name</h1>

        @if (_flashMessage is not null)
        {
            <p class="status-success" role="status">@_flashMessage</p>
        }
        @if (_errorMessage is not null)
        {
            <p class="status-error" role="alert">@_errorMessage</p>
        }

        <div class="manage-facts">
            <div>
                <span class="manage-label">Availability</span>
                @if (_item.IsActive)
                {
                    <span class="chip chip-ok">Available</span>

                else
                {
                    <span class="chip chip-warn">Currently unavailable</span>

            </div>

        <hr class="manage-rule" />

        <h2 class="manage-heading">Name</h2>
        <p class="lede">
            Renaming shows through everywhere immediately, including on lines already sent and on closed
            bills — the name is read at display time, not captured (§8.3). Rename to correct a spelling;
            create a second item if it is a different dish.
        </p>
        <EditForm Model="RenameInput" method="post" OnValidSubmit="RenameAsync" FormName="menu-item-rename" class="manage-inline-form">

            <label class="visually-hidden" for="rename-name">New name</label>
            <InputText id="rename-name" @bind-Value="RenameInput.Name" autocomplete="off" />
            <button type="submit" class="button-primary">Rename</button>
            <ValidationMessage For="@(() => RenameInput.Name)" />
        </EditForm>

        <hr class="manage-rule" />

        <h2 class="manage-heading">Price</h2>
        <p class="lede">
            A new price applies to lines added <strong>from now on</strong>. Anything already on an order
            keeps the price it was added at, including on open tables — that is the capture rule (§6.5.4),
            and it is why a guest who ordered before the change is not surprised at the till.
        </p>
        <EditForm Model="RepriceInput" method="post" OnValidSubmit="RepriceAsync" FormName="menu-item-reprice" class="manage-inline-form">
            <DataAnnotationsValidator />
            <label class="visually-hidden" for="reprice-price">New price</label>
            <span class="manage-currency">@Options.CurrencyCode</span>

        </EditForm>

        }

        <p class="manage-back"><a href="/administration/menu">Back to the menu</a></p>

@code {
    private MenuItemSummary? _item;
    private IReadOnlyList<MenuItemEventEntry>? _history;
    private string? _flashMessage;
    private string? _errorMessage;

    [Parameter]
    public Guid MenuItemId { get; set; }

    [CascadingParameter]
    private HttpContext HttpContext { get; set; } = default!;

    [SupplyParameterFromForm(FormName = "menu-item-rename")]
    private RenameInputModel RenameInput { get; set; } = default!;

    [SupplyParameterFromForm(FormName = "menu-item-reprice")]
    private RepriceInputModel RepriceInput { get; set; } = default!;

    [SupplyParameterFromQuery]
    private string? Done { get; set; }

    private string ManagePath => $"/administration/menu/{MenuItemId}";

    protected override async Task OnInitializedAsync()
    {
        // BL0008: a form POST binds these itself and may assign null, so the defaults live here.
        RenameInput ??= new();
        RepriceInput ??= new();

        _item = await MenuItems.GetAsync(MenuItemId, HttpContext.RequestAborted);
        if (_item is null)
        {
            return;
        }

        _history = await MenuEvents.ListForItemAsync(MenuItemId, HttpContext.RequestAborted);

        // On GET, pre-fill both editors with what is stored and render any post/redirect flash. On POST
        // the submitted values are already bound, so they must not be overwritten.
        if (HttpMethods.IsGet(HttpContext.Request.Method))
        {
            if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(RenameInput.Name))
            {
                RenameInput.Name = _item.Name;
            }

            RepriceInput.PriceAmount = _item.PriceAmount;
            _flashMessage = FlashFor(Done);
        }
    }

    private async Task RenameAsync()
    {
        if (!TryBegin(out Guid administrator))
        {
            return;
        }

        RenameMenuItemResult result = await MenuChanges.RenameMenuItemAsync(
            MenuItemId, RenameInput.Name.Trim(), administrator, HttpContext.RequestAborted);

        switch (result.Outcome)
        {
            case RenameMenuItemOutcome.Renamed:
                RedirectWithOutcome("renamed");
                break;
            case RenameMenuItemOutcome.NoChange:
                RedirectWithOutcome("rename-no-change");
                break;
            case RenameMenuItemOutcome.MenuItemNotFound:
                Navigation.NavigateTo("/administration/menu");
                break;
        }
    }

    private async Task RepriceAsync()
    {
        if (!TryBegin(out Guid administrator))
        {
            return;
        }

        RepriceMenuItemResult result = await MenuChanges.RepriceMenuItemAsync(
            MenuItemId, RepriceInput.PriceAmount, administrator, HttpContext.RequestAborted);

        switch (result.Outcome)
        {
            case RepriceMenuItemOutcome.Repriced:
                RedirectWithOutcome("repriced");
                break;
            case RepriceMenuItemOutcome.NoChange:
                RedirectWithOutcome("reprice-no-change");
                break;
            case RepriceMenuItemOutcome.MenuItemNotFound:
                Navigation.NavigateTo("/administration/menu");
                break;
        }
    }

    private async Task ToggleAvailabilityAsync()
    {
        if (_item is null || !TryBegin(out Guid administrator))
        {
            return;
        }

        bool target = !_item.IsActive;
        SetMenuItemAvailabilityResult result = await MenuChanges.SetMenuItemActiveAsync(
            MenuItemId, target, administrator, HttpContext.RequestAborted);

        switch (result.Outcome)
        {
            case SetMenuItemAvailabilityOutcome.Changed:
                RedirectWithOutcome(target ? "made-available" : "made-unavailable");
                break;
            case SetMenuItemAvailabilityOutcome.AlreadyInThatState:
                // Somebody in the kitchen got there first between this page rendering and the button
                // being pressed. Nothing changed and nothing is wrong; re-render on the truth.
                Navigation.NavigateTo(ManagePath);
                break;
            case SetMenuItemAvailabilityOutcome.MenuItemNotFound:
                Navigation.NavigateTo("/administration/menu");
                break;
        }
    }

    /// <summary>
    /// The two things every write on this page needs first: the item must still exist, and the acting
    /// administrator must be identifiable — <c>menu_item_event.actor_person_identifier</c> is NOT NULL and
    /// §7 requires every change to name somebody. Endpoint authorization already guarantees the second;
    /// this is the belt to that brace.
    /// </summary>
    private bool TryBegin(out Guid administrator)
    {
        administrator = Guid.Empty;

        if (_item is null)
        {
            Navigation.NavigateTo("/administration/menu");
            return false;
        }

        if (PersonPrincipal.IdentifierFor(HttpContext.User) is not { } identifier)
        {
            _errorMessage = "Your session could not be identified. Sign in again and retry.";
            return false;
        }

        administrator = identifier;
        return true;
    }

    private void RedirectWithOutcome(string outcome)
        => Navigation.NavigateTo($"{ManagePath}?done={outcome}");

    private static string? FlashFor(string? outcome) => outcome switch
    {
        "renamed" => "Renamed. The new name shows everywhere immediately, including on past orders.",
        "rename-no-change" => "That was already the name — nothing changed.",
        "repriced" => "Repriced. Lines already on an order keep the price they were added at.",
        "reprice-no-change" => "That was already the price — nothing changed.",
        "made-unavailable" => "Marked unavailable. It stays on the guest's menu, labelled unavailable, and cannot be ordered.",
        "made-available" => "Marked available. It can be ordered again.",
        _ => null,
    };

    private string Money(decimal amount) => MoneyText.Format(amount, Options.CurrencyCode);

    /// <summary>
    /// A friendly label for the five event types §8.2's CHECK admits, falling back to the stored string
    /// for anything else — §11.4 renders the record, so an unrecognised type must show as itself rather
    /// than be swallowed.
    /// </summary>
    private string Describe(MenuItemEventEntry entry) => entry.EventType switch
    {
        "created" => $"Created as “{entry.NewName}” at {Money(entry.NewPriceAmount ?? 0m)}",
        "name_changed" => $"Renamed to “{entry.NewName}”",
        "price_changed" => $"Repriced to {Money(entry.NewPriceAmount ?? 0m)}",
        "activated" => "Marked available",
        "deactivated" => "Marked unavailable",
        _ => entry.EventType,
    };

    private sealed class RenameInputModel
    {
        [Required(ErrorMessage = "Enter a name.")]
        [StringLength(120, MinimumLength = 1, ErrorMessage = "The name must be 1–120 characters.")]
        public string Name { get; set; } = string.Empty;
    }

    private sealed class RepriceInputModel
    {
        [Range(0, 99999999.99, ErrorMessage = "The price must be between 0 and 99,999,999.99.")]
        public decimal PriceAmount { get; set; }
    }
}

@* Manage one account (TECHNICAL_SPECIFICATION §3.7). Administrator only (endpoint authorization).
   Static SSR: grant/revoke, reset, and deactivate/reactivate are full-page form posts, and the reset's
   temporary password is written into the response once and never stored in the clear. Each action runs
   through the transactional IAccountAdministration, which rotates the subject's security stamp so the
   change bites their live sessions within the revalidation window (§3.1). Successful changes redirect
   back here (post/redirect/get) carrying a one-word outcome so a refresh does not re-post; refusals
   (last administrator) are shown in place. *@

@code {
    private static readonly string[] AllStaffRoles =
        [RestaurantRoles.Administrator, RestaurantRoles.Counter, RestaurantRoles.Kitchen];

    private PersonSummary? _person;
    private IReadOnlyList<string> _grantableRoles = [];
    private bool _isSelf;
    private string? _flashMessage;
    private string? _errorMessage;

    private CredentialResetResult? _resetResult;
    private string? _temporaryPassword;

    [Parameter]
    public Guid PersonId { get; set; }

    [CascadingParameter]
    private HttpContext HttpContext { get; set; } = default!;

    [SupplyParameterFromForm(FormName = "manage-grant-role")]
    private RoleSelectionModel GrantInput { get; set; } = default!;

    [SupplyParameterFromForm(FormName = "manage-revoke-role")]
    private RoleSelectionModel RevokeInput { get; set; } = default!;

    [SupplyParameterFromQuery]
    private string? Done { get; set; }

    private string ManagePath => $"/administration/people/{PersonId}";

    protected override async Task OnInitializedAsync()
    {
        // BL0008: form POSTs bind these themselves and may assign null, so defaults live here.
        GrantInput ??= new();
        RevokeInput ??= new();

        _person = await People.GetPersonAsync(PersonId, HttpContext.RequestAborted);
        if (_person is null)
        {
            return;
        }

        _grantableRoles = AllStaffRoles.Where(role => !_person.Roles.Contains(role)).ToArray();

        Person? actingAdministrator = await UserManager.GetUserAsync(HttpContext.User);
        _isSelf = actingAdministrator is not null && actingAdministrator.PersonIdentifier == _person.PersonIdentifier;

        // Render the flash for a completed action after the post/redirect/get, on GET only.
        if (HttpContext.Request.Method == HttpMethods.Get)
        {
            _flashMessage = FlashFor(Done);
        }
    }

    private async Task GrantRoleAsync()
    {
        if (_person is null)
        {
            Navigation.NavigateTo("/administration");
            return;
        }

        Person? admin = await UserManager.GetUserAsync(HttpContext.User);
        if (admin is null)
        {
            Navigation.NavigateTo(AccountRoutes.SignIn);
            return;
        }

        if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(GrantInput.RoleName))
        {
            _errorMessage = "Choose a role to grant.";
            return;
        }

        RoleGrantOutcome outcome = await Accounts.GrantRoleAsync(
            _person.PersonIdentifier, GrantInput.RoleName, admin.PersonIdentifier, HttpContext.RequestAborted);

        switch (outcome)
        {
            case RoleGrantOutcome.Granted:
                RedirectWithOutcome("role-granted");
                break;
            case RoleGrantOutcome.AlreadyHeld:
                RedirectWithOutcome("role-already-held");
                break;
            case RoleGrantOutcome.PersonNotFound:
                Navigation.NavigateTo(ManagePath);
                break;
        }
    }

    private async Task RevokeRoleAsync()
    {
        if (_person is null)
        {
            Navigation.NavigateTo("/administration");
            return;
        }

        Person? admin = await UserManager.GetUserAsync(HttpContext.User);
        if (admin is null)
        {
            Navigation.NavigateTo(AccountRoutes.SignIn);
            return;
        }

        if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(RevokeInput.RoleName))
        {
            _errorMessage = "Choose a role to revoke.";
            return;
        }

        RoleRevokeOutcome outcome = await Accounts.RevokeRoleAsync(
            _person.PersonIdentifier, RevokeInput.RoleName, admin.PersonIdentifier, HttpContext.RequestAborted);

        switch (outcome)
        {
            case RoleRevokeOutcome.Revoked:
                RedirectWithOutcome("role-revoked");
                break;
            case RoleRevokeOutcome.NotHeld:
                RedirectWithOutcome("role-not-held");
                break;
            case RoleRevokeOutcome.WouldRemoveLastAdministrator:
                _errorMessage = "This is the only administrator, so the administrator role cannot be removed. "
                    + "Grant administrator to someone else first.";
                break;
            case RoleRevokeOutcome.PersonNotFound:
                Navigation.NavigateTo(ManagePath);
                break;
        }
    }

    private async Task ResetCredentialsAsync()
    {
        if (_person is null)
        {
            Navigation.NavigateTo("/administration");
            return;
        }

        Person? admin = await UserManager.GetUserAsync(HttpContext.User);
        if (admin is null)
        {
            Navigation.NavigateTo(AccountRoutes.SignIn);
            return;
        }

        // Generate + hash the temporary password here so the plaintext is only ever held for the one
        // response that shows it (§3.2). 12 random bytes → a 16-character URL-safe string.
        string temporaryPassword = SecretGenerator.GenerateBase64UrlSecret(12);
        string passwordHash = PasswordHasher.HashPassword(
            new Person { PersonIdentifier = _person.PersonIdentifier, Username = _person.Username },
            temporaryPassword);

        CredentialResetResult result = await Accounts.ResetCredentialsAsync(
            _person.PersonIdentifier, passwordHash, admin.PersonIdentifier, HttpContext.RequestAborted);

        if (result.Outcome == CredentialResetOutcome.PersonNotFound)
        {
            Navigation.NavigateTo(ManagePath);
            return;
        }

        // Show the temporary password once, in this response (no redirect).
        _temporaryPassword = temporaryPassword;
        _resetResult = result;
    }

    private async Task ToggleActivationAsync()
    {
        if (_person is null)
        {
            Navigation.NavigateTo("/administration");
            return;
        }

        Person? admin = await UserManager.GetUserAsync(HttpContext.User);
        if (admin is null)
        {
            Navigation.NavigateTo(AccountRoutes.SignIn);
            return;
        }

        bool target = !_person.IsActive;
        AccountActivationOutcome outcome = await Accounts.SetAccountActiveAsync(
            _person.PersonIdentifier, target, admin.PersonIdentifier, HttpContext.RequestAborted);

        switch (outcome)
        {
            case AccountActivationOutcome.Changed:
                RedirectWithOutcome(target ? "account-reactivated" : "account-deactivated");
                break;
            case AccountActivationOutcome.NoChange:
                Navigation.NavigateTo(ManagePath);
                break;
            case AccountActivationOutcome.WouldDeactivateLastAdministrator:
                _errorMessage = "This is the only administrator that can sign in, so it cannot be deactivated. "
                    + "Make sure another administrator is active first.";
                break;
            case AccountActivationOutcome.PersonNotFound:
                Navigation.NavigateTo(ManagePath);
                break;
        }
    }

    private void RedirectWithOutcome(string outcome)
        => Navigation.NavigateTo($"{ManagePath}?done={outcome}");

    private static string? FlashFor(string? outcome) => outcome switch
    {
        "role-granted" => "Role granted. It takes effect on their sessions within a few minutes.",
        "role-already-held" => "That role was already held — nothing changed.",
        "role-revoked" => "Role revoked. It takes effect on their sessions within a few minutes.",
        "role-not-held" => "That role was not held — nothing changed.",
        "account-deactivated" => "Account deactivated. Its sessions end within a few minutes.",
        "account-reactivated" => "Account reactivated.",
        _ => null,
    };

    private bool IsLockedOut(PersonSummary person)
        => person.LockoutEndAt is { } end && end > Clock.UtcNow;

    private static string Capitalize(string role)
        => string.IsNullOrEmpty(role) ? role : char.ToUpperInvariant(role[0]) + role[1..];

    private sealed class RoleSelectionModel
    {
        public string RoleName { get; set; } = string.Empty;
    }
}

@page "/administration/sittings/{SittingId:guid}"
@attribute [ExcludeFromInteractiveRouting]
@attribute [Authorize(Policy = AuthorizationPolicies.Administration)]
@using MyRestaurant.DataAccess.Menu
@using MyRestaurant.DataAccess.Orders
@using MyRestaurant.DataAccess.Sittings

@inject ICounterBoardReads CounterReads
@inject ISittingRecordReads SittingRecords
@inject IOrderReadModel OrderReads
@inject ISittingDirectory SittingDirectory
@inject IMenuDirectory MenuItems
@inject IOrderWorkflow Workflow
@inject IIdentifierFactory Identifiers
@inject RestaurantOptions Options
@inject RestaurantTime RestaurantClock
@inject NavigationManager Navigation

@* One sitting's complete stored record, and the corrections an administrator may append to it
   (TECHNICAL_SPECIFICATION §5.3, §6.7, §11.4).

   §11.4 is emphatic about what this page owes its reader: "Administration renders the complete stored
   record everywhere — full event streams, visibility logs, security events — never projected or truncated
   for the administrator; filters narrow only on explicit request." So the history below is every event on
   every order in the sitting, oldest first, uncapped, including the removals, the reverted fulfillments,
   and the prices that were superseded. A settled bill is the thing people argue about, and an argument is
   settled by reading forward from the first send.

   Static SSR, like every administration surface. Corrections are full-page form posts that redirect back
   here (post/redirect/get) carrying a one-word outcome, so a refresh cannot re-append.

   **The corrective controls appear only once the sitting is settled.** §6.7 is titled "post-close
   corrections" and §3.7's matrix gives "post-close corrective events" to the administrator alone; while a
   table is still eating, the screen built for it is the counter's, and an administrator already holds the
   counter role's capabilities (§3.7), so this page links there instead of growing a second copy of it.
   The record itself renders either way — an administrator reading an open table's history is not a write. *@

<PageTitle>@(_sitting is null ? "Sitting record" : $"Sitting — {_sitting.TableLabel}")</PageTitle>

@if (_sitting is null)
{
    <section class="panel">
        <p class="eyebrow">Administration</p>

        <p class="lede">No sitting exists with that identifier. It may have never existed, or the link is stale.</p>
        <p><a href="/administration/sittings">Back to sittings</a></p>
    </section>
}
else
{
    <section class="panel sitting-record">
        <p class="eyebrow">Administration — sittings</p>

        <div class="admin-header">
            <div>

                    @_sitting.MemberCount @(_sitting.MemberCount == 1 ? "guest" : "guests") ·

            </div>

                @if (_sitting.HasPostCloseCorrections)

                }

        </div>

        @if (_flashMessage is not null)

        }

                </p>

        @* ---- the complete stored record (§11.4) -------------------------------------------------- *@
        <hr class="sitting-rule" />

        <h2 class="sitting-heading">The record</h2>

        @if (_records.Count == 0)
        {

            </p>

        else
        {
            <p class="lede">
                Every event on every order, oldest first and complete — @_eventCount in total. Removed
                lines, undone fulfillments, and superseded prices are all still here, because the history

            </p>

            @foreach (SittingOrderRecord orderRecord in _records)
            {
                <article class="sitting-order">
                    <header class="sitting-order-header">
                        <h3>@orderRecord.OwnerName</h3>
                        <span class="muted">
                            order opened @RestaurantClock.DateAndTime(orderRecord.CreatedAt) ·

                        </span>
                    </header>

                    @if (orderRecord.Events.Count == 0)
                    {
                        <p class="muted">
                            The order row exists with no events on it. Only reachable if a write created it
                            and then rolled back its event, which the transaction does not do — worth
                            reporting if you are seeing it.
                        </p>
                    }
                    else
                    {
                        <ol class="sitting-events">
                            @foreach (StoredOrderEvent stored in orderRecord.Events)
                            {
                                <li class="sitting-event">
                                    <div class="sitting-event-head">
                                        <span class="sitting-event-sequence">#@stored.SequenceNumber</span>
                                        <span class="sitting-event-type">@DescribeEventType(stored.EventType)</span>
                                        <span class="muted">
                                            @stored.ActorName as @DescribeActorRole(stored.ActorRole) ·
                                            @RestaurantClock.DateAndTimeWithSeconds(stored.OccurredAt)
                                        </span>
                                    </div>

                                    @if (stored.Operations.Count == 0)
                                    {
                                        <p class="muted">
                                            No operations recorded, which §6.5.1 forbids — worth reporting.
                                        </p>
                                    }
                                    else
                                    {
                                        <ul class="sitting-operations">
                                            @foreach (StoredOrderOperation operation in stored.Operations)
                                            {
                                                <li>@DescribeOperation(operation)</li>
                                            }
                                        </ul>
                                    }
                                </li>
                            }
                        </ol>
                    }
                </article>
            }
        }

        <p><a href="/administration/sittings">Back to sittings</a></p>
    </section>
}

@code {
    /// <summary>Somebody a correction can be billed to: a member, or anyone who already has an order here.</summary>
    private sealed record BillablePerson(Guid PersonIdentifier, string Name);

    /// <summary>
    /// The two things the one correction form can do. They are two different §6.2 event types with two
    /// different operation subtypes, so they cannot be one Save — but they are one form, because a
    /// per-line panel would need a distinct form name per row and static SSR has no model to bind
    /// a dynamic set of them to. This is the shape TableDisplays and CounterSitting already use: one
    /// picker, at the bottom, that can name any row above it.
    /// </summary>
    private const string AdjustAction = "adjust";

    private const string RemoveAction = "remove";

    private CounterSittingSummary? _sitting;
    private IReadOnlyList<SittingMemberSummary> _members = [];
    private IReadOnlyList<SittingBillEntry> _bill = [];
    private IReadOnlyList<OrderLineView> _lines = [];
    private IReadOnlyList<SittingOrderRecord> _records = [];
    private IReadOnlyList<MenuItemSummary> _menu = [];
    private IReadOnlyList<BillablePerson> _peopleAtTheTable = [];
    private int _eventCount;

    private string? _flashMessage;
    private string? _errorMessage;
    private IReadOnlyList<string> _rejectionReasons = [];

    /// <summary>The sitting this page reports on. Every query is scoped by it, never by the table.</summary>
    [Parameter]
    public Guid SittingId { get; set; }

    [CascadingParameter]
    private HttpContext HttpContext { get; set; } = default!;

    [SupplyParameterFromForm(FormName = "sitting-correct-line")]
    private CorrectLineInputModel CorrectInput { get; set; } = default!;

    [SupplyParameterFromForm(FormName = "sitting-add-line")]
    private AddLineInputModel AddInput { get; set; } = default!;

    [SupplyParameterFromQuery]
    private string? Done { get; set; }

    private string RecordPath => $"/administration/sittings/{SittingId}";

    private string CounterPath => $"/counter/sittings/{SittingId}";

    private decimal TableTotal => _bill.Sum(entry => entry.PersonTotalAmount);

    /// <summary>The " · settled 9:14 PM by Cass" tail of the header line, built here because it reads as one sentence.</summary>
    private string SettledSuffix
    {
        get
        {
            if (_sitting is not { ClosedAt: { } closedAt })
            {
                return string.Empty;
            }

            string by = string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(_sitting.ClosedByName)
                ? string.Empty
                : $" by {_sitting.ClosedByName}";

            return $" · settled {RestaurantClock.DateAndTime(closedAt)}{by}";
        }
    }

    protected override async Task OnInitializedAsync()
    {
        // BL0008: a form POST binds these itself and may assign null, so the defaults live here.
        CorrectInput ??= new();
        AddInput ??= new();

        await LoadAsync();

        if (_sitting is null)
        {
            return;
        }

        if (HttpMethods.IsGet(HttpContext.Request.Method))
        {
            CorrectInput.Action = AdjustAction;
            AddInput.Quantity = 1;
            _flashMessage = FlashFor(Done);
        }
    }

    /// <summary>Everything the page shows, re-read in one pass. Small, indexed queries.</summary>
    private async Task LoadAsync()
    {
        CancellationToken cancellationToken = HttpContext.RequestAborted;

        _sitting = await CounterReads.GetSittingAsync(SittingId, cancellationToken);

        if (_sitting is null)
        {
            _members = [];
            _bill = [];
            _lines = [];
            _records = [];
            _menu = [];
            _peopleAtTheTable = [];
            _eventCount = 0;
            return;
        }

        _members = await SittingDirectory.ListMembersAsync(SittingId, cancellationToken);
        _bill = await OrderReads.ListSittingBillAsync(SittingId, cancellationToken);
        _lines = await OrderReads.ListLinesForSittingAsync(SittingId, cancellationToken);
        _records = await SittingRecords.ListOrderRecordsForSittingAsync(SittingId, cancellationToken);
        _menu = await MenuItems.ListAsync(cancellationToken);

        _eventCount = _records.Sum(order => order.Events.Count);
        _peopleAtTheTable = BuildPeopleAtTheTable();
    }

    /// <summary>
    /// The roster, plus anybody who has an order without a membership row. The union rather than the
    /// roster alone, because the picker must never be unable to name somebody whose bill is on the screen
    /// directly above it.
    /// </summary>
    private IReadOnlyList<BillablePerson> BuildPeopleAtTheTable()
    {
        List<BillablePerson> people = _members
            .Select(member => new BillablePerson(member.PersonIdentifier, member.RosterName))
            .ToList();

        foreach (SittingBillEntry entry in _bill)
        {
            if (!people.Any(person => person.PersonIdentifier == entry.PersonIdentifier))
            {
                people.Add(new BillablePerson(entry.PersonIdentifier, entry.BillName));
            }
        }

        return people;
    }

    /// <summary>§6.7 through §6.5.8: an administrator's corrective price change or removal on a settled bill.</summary>
    private async Task CorrectLineAsync()
    {
        if (!TryBegin(out Guid administrator))
        {
            return;
        }

        if (!Guid.TryParse(CorrectInput.OrderLineIdentifier, out Guid orderLineIdentifier))
        {
            _errorMessage = "Choose which line to correct.";
            return;
        }

        OrderLineView? line = _lines
            .FirstOrDefault(candidate => candidate.OrderLineIdentifier == orderLineIdentifier);

        if (line is null)
        {
            // Somebody corrected it between this page rendering and the button being pressed. Re-read and
            // say so rather than sending an operation the transaction would refuse anyway.
            _errorMessage = "That line is no longer on the bill. The record below has been refreshed.";
            await LoadAsync();
            return;
        }

        if (CorrectInput.Action == RemoveAction)
        {
            await AppendAsync(
                administrator,
                line.GuestOrderIdentifier,
                OrderEventType.StaffEdit,
                [new LineRemovedOperation(orderLineIdentifier, Blank(CorrectInput.Reason))],
                "line-removed");
            return;
        }

        if (CorrectInput.Action != AdjustAction)
        {
            _errorMessage = "Choose whether to change the price or take the line off the bill.";
            return;
        }

        if (string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(CorrectInput.Reason))
        {
            _errorMessage = "A price change needs a reason — it is the sentence somebody reads back later.";
            return;
        }

        if (CorrectInput.NewUnitPriceAmount < 0m)
        {
            _errorMessage = "A price cannot be negative.";
            return;
        }

        // Rounded once, here, away from zero — matching numeric(10,2)'s own rule — so the operation row,
        // the projection, and the number reported back are the same value rather than three independent
        // roundings of the same input. The same decision MenuAdministration made for reprice.
        decimal newUnitPrice = Math.Round(CorrectInput.NewUnitPriceAmount, 2, MidpointRounding.AwayFromZero);

        await AppendAsync(
            administrator,
            line.GuestOrderIdentifier,
            OrderEventType.PriceAdjustment,
            [new LinePriceAdjustedOperation(orderLineIdentifier, newUnitPrice, CorrectInput.Reason.Trim())],
            "line-repriced");
    }

    /// <summary>
    /// §6.7's other half: a plate that went out and was never billed. Routed through the living-order path
    /// so it works for somebody who joined and never sent anything — their order row is created inside the
    /// same transaction (§6.1), which is not something this surface can do for itself.
    /// </summary>
    private async Task AddLineAsync()
    {
        if (!TryBegin(out Guid administrator))
        {
            return;
        }

        if (!Guid.TryParse(AddInput.PersonIdentifier, out Guid personIdentifier)
            || _peopleAtTheTable.All(person => person.PersonIdentifier != personIdentifier))
        {
            _errorMessage = "Choose which guest this line belongs to.";
            return;
        }

        if (!Guid.TryParse(AddInput.MenuItemIdentifier, out Guid menuItemIdentifier))
        {
            _errorMessage = "Choose an item to add.";
            return;
        }

        MenuItemSummary? item = _menu
            .FirstOrDefault(candidate => candidate.MenuItemIdentifier == menuItemIdentifier);

        if (item is null)
        {
            _errorMessage = "That item is no longer on the menu.";
            return;
        }

        // §7 keeps a deactivated item visible and unorderable; the transaction re-checks the flag under
        // its own lock (§6.5.4), so this only makes the answer immediate.
        if (!item.IsActive)
        {
            _errorMessage =
                $"{item.Name} is currently marked unavailable, so it cannot be added. Make it available first.";
            return;
        }

        if (AddInput.Quantity is < 1 or > 100)
        {
            _errorMessage = "Quantity must be between 1 and 100.";
            return;
        }

        // The line's own identity, UUIDv7 like every other key (ADR-0011). The unit price passed here is
        // ignored: the transaction prices the line from the menu row it reads under the lock (§6.5.4).
        LineAddedOperation added = new(
            Identifiers.Create(),
            menuItemIdentifier,
            AddInput.Quantity,
            item.PriceAmount,
            Blank(AddInput.Note));

        AppendOrderEventResult result = await Workflow.AppendStaffEventToLivingOrderAsync(
            SittingId,
            personIdentifier,
            new ProposedOrderEvent(
                OrderEventType.StaffEdit,
                administrator,
                OrderActorRole.Administrator,
                [added]),
            HttpContext.RequestAborted);

        await ReportAsync(result, "line-added");
    }

    private async Task AppendAsync(
        Guid administrator,
        Guid guestOrderIdentifier,
        OrderEventType eventType,
        IReadOnlyList<OrderOperation> operations,
        string outcome)
    {
        AppendOrderEventResult result = await Workflow.AppendStaffEventAsync(
            guestOrderIdentifier,
            new ProposedOrderEvent(eventType, administrator, OrderActorRole.Administrator, operations),
            HttpContext.RequestAborted);

        await ReportAsync(result, outcome);
    }

    /// <summary>
    /// Redirect on success so a refresh cannot re-append; render the refusal in place on failure, because
    /// the per-operation reasons §6.5.9 produces do not survive a query string and are the whole value of
    /// the message.
    /// </summary>
    private async Task ReportAsync(AppendOrderEventResult result, string outcome)
    {
        if (result.IsAppended)
        {
            Navigation.NavigateTo($"{RecordPath}?done={outcome}");
            return;
        }

        _errorMessage = DescribeRefusal(result);
        _rejectionReasons = result.Errors.Select(error => error.Reason).ToArray();
        await LoadAsync();
    }

    private static string DescribeRefusal(AppendOrderEventResult result) => result.Outcome switch
    {
        AppendOrderEventOutcome.SittingNotFound => "That sitting no longer exists. Nothing was written.",
        AppendOrderEventOutcome.OrderNotFound => "There is no order here to append to. Nothing was written.",
        _ => "Nothing was written. The record below has been refreshed.",
    };

    /// <summary>
    /// The sitting must still exist and the acting administrator must be identifiable —
    /// <c>order_event.actor_person_identifier</c> is NOT NULL and §6.2 requires every event to name
    /// somebody. Endpoint authorization already guarantees the second; this is the belt to that brace.
    /// Also refuses on an open sitting, which the markup does not offer but a replayed post could.
    /// </summary>
    private bool TryBegin(out Guid administrator)
    {
        administrator = Guid.Empty;

        if (_sitting is null)
        {
            Navigation.NavigateTo("/administration/sittings");
            return false;
        }

        if (_sitting.IsOpen)
        {
            _errorMessage =
                "This table is still open, so there is nothing to correct. Settle it at the counter first.";
            return false;
        }

        if (PersonPrincipal.IdentifierFor(HttpContext.User) is not { } identifier)
        {
            _errorMessage = "Your session could not be identified. Sign in again and retry.";
            return false;
        }

        administrator = identifier;
        return true;
    }

    private bool HasAnOrder(Guid personIdentifier)
        => _bill.Any(entry => entry.PersonIdentifier == personIdentifier);

    private IReadOnlyList<OrderLineView> LinesFor(Guid guestOrderIdentifier)
        => _lines.Where(line => line.GuestOrderIdentifier == guestOrderIdentifier).ToArray();

    private string LineOptionLabel(OrderLineView line)
        => $"{OwnerNameFor(line.GuestOrderIdentifier)} — {line.Quantity} × {line.MenuItemName} " +
           $"at {Money(line.CurrentUnitPriceAmount)}";

    private string OwnerNameFor(Guid guestOrderIdentifier)
    {
        SittingBillEntry? entry = _bill
            .FirstOrDefault(candidate => candidate.GuestOrderIdentifier == guestOrderIdentifier);

        if (entry is not null)
        {
            return entry.BillName;
        }

        SittingOrderRecord? orderRecord = _records
            .FirstOrDefault(candidate => candidate.GuestOrderIdentifier == guestOrderIdentifier);

        return orderRecord?.OwnerName ?? "Unknown guest";
    }

    private string ItemOptionLabel(MenuItemSummary item)
        => item.IsActive
            ? $"{item.Name} — {Money(item.PriceAmount)}"
            : $"{item.Name} — {Money(item.PriceAmount)} (currently unavailable)";

    /// <summary>
    /// A friendly label for the five <c>order_event.event_type</c> values §8.2's CHECK admits, falling
    /// back to the stored string for anything else. The words are spelled out here rather than taken from
    /// <c>OrderEventVocabulary</c>, which is internal to the data-access assembly on purpose — a display
    /// label is not the writer's business, and a reader that threw on an unrecognised word would blank the
    /// one page whose job is to show what is actually stored. Same shape as ManageMenuItem's.
    /// </summary>
    private static string DescribeEventType(string eventType) => eventType switch
    {
        "guest_submission" => "Guest send",
        "staff_edit" => "Staff edit",
        "price_adjustment" => "Price change",
        "fulfillment" => "Delivered",
        "fulfillment_reversal" => "Delivery undone",
        _ => eventType,
    };

    /// <summary>
    /// The four <c>order_event.actor_role</c> values, on the same terms. <c>guest</c> is a capacity rather
    /// than a stored role (§0, §3.7) — an administrator eating lunch appears here as a guest, and that is
    /// correct.
    /// </summary>
    private static string DescribeActorRole(string actorRole) => actorRole switch
    {
        "guest" => "a guest",
        "kitchen" => "the kitchen",
        "counter" => "the counter",
        "administrator" => "an administrator",
        _ => actorRole,
    };

    /// <summary>
    /// One stored operation in a sentence. The five kinds are the discriminators the reader's UNION
    /// projects; an unknown one renders as itself beside the line it names, so nothing is ever swallowed.
    /// </summary>
    private string DescribeOperation(StoredOrderOperation operation) => operation.OperationKind switch
    {
        "line_added" =>
            $"Added {operation.Quantity} × {operation.MenuItemName} at " +
            $"{Money(operation.UnitPriceAmount ?? 0m)} each{NoteSuffix(operation.CustomizationNote)}",
        "line_removed" =>
            $"Removed {operation.Quantity} × {operation.MenuItemName}{ReasonSuffix(operation.Reason)}",
        "line_price_adjusted" =>
            $"{operation.Quantity} × {operation.MenuItemName} repriced to " +
            $"{Money(operation.NewUnitPriceAmount ?? 0m)} each{ReasonSuffix(operation.Reason)}",
        "line_fulfilled" =>
            $"{operation.Quantity} × {operation.MenuItemName} delivered",
        "line_fulfillment_reverted" =>
            $"{operation.Quantity} × {operation.MenuItemName} put back with the kitchen",
        _ => $"{operation.OperationKind} on {operation.Quantity} × {operation.MenuItemName}",
    };

    private static string NoteSuffix(string? note)
        => string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(note) ? string.Empty : $" — “{note.Trim()}”";

    private static string ReasonSuffix(string? reason)
        => string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(reason) ? string.Empty : $" — {reason.Trim()}";

    private static string? FlashFor(string? outcome) => outcome switch
    {
        "line-repriced" =>
            "Price changed. The settled total above is unchanged — the correction shows beside it.",
        "line-removed" =>
            "Line taken off the bill. It stays in the record with your name and the reason; it simply stops being charged.",
        "line-added" =>
            "Line added. It appears in the corrected total, not in the settled one, which is never rewritten.",
        _ => null,
    };

    private static string? Blank(string? value)
        => string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(value) ? null : value.Trim();

    private string Money(decimal amount) => MoneyText.Format(amount, Options.CurrencyCode);

    private sealed class CorrectLineInputModel
    {
        [Required(ErrorMessage = "Choose which line to correct.")]
        public string OrderLineIdentifier { get; set; } = string.Empty;

        [Required(ErrorMessage = "Choose what to do.")]
        public string Action { get; set; } = string.Empty;

        [Range(0, 99999999.99, ErrorMessage = "The price must be between 0 and 99,999,999.99.")]
        public decimal NewUnitPriceAmount { get; set; }

        [StringLength(200, ErrorMessage = "A reason must be 200 characters or fewer.")]
        public string? Reason { get; set; }
    }

    private sealed class AddLineInputModel
    {
        [Required(ErrorMessage = "Choose which guest this line belongs to.")]
        public string PersonIdentifier { get; set; } = string.Empty;

        [Required(ErrorMessage = "Choose an item to add.")]
        public string MenuItemIdentifier { get; set; } = string.Empty;

        [Range(1, 100, ErrorMessage = "Quantity must be between 1 and 100.")]
        public int Quantity { get; set; } = 1;

        [StringLength(500, ErrorMessage = "A note must be 500 characters or fewer.")]
        public string? Note { get; set; }
    }
}

@page "/administration/tables/{TableId:guid}"
@attribute [ExcludeFromInteractiveRouting]
@attribute [Authorize(Policy = AuthorizationPolicies.Administration)]
@using MyRestaurant.DataAccess.Tables
@inject ITableDirectory TableDirectory
@inject ITableAdministration Tables
@inject NavigationManager Navigation
@inject RestaurantTime RestaurantClock

@* Manage one table (TECHNICAL_SPECIFICATION §4.1). Administrator only (endpoint authorization).
   Static SSR: rename, rotate-secret, and deactivate/reactivate are full-page form posts. Successful
   changes redirect back here (post/redirect/get) carrying a one-word outcome so a refresh does not
   re-post; a taken label is shown in place. The join secret is never read or shown — rotation replaces
   it server-side (§4.1). A link to the join-code fallback (§4.5) sits alongside, for when a table's
   display is down, and a link to this table's display devices (§4.2) for pairing and revoking them. *@
