    <section class="panel account-panel">
        <p class="eyebrow">First-run setup</p>

        <ol class="setup-steps" aria-label="Setup progress">
            <li class="@StepClass(0)">Account</li>
            <li class="@StepClass(1)">Passkey</li>
            <li class="@StepClass(2)">Authenticator</li>
            <li class="@StepClass(3)">Finish</li>
        </ol>

        @if (_errorMessage is not null)
        {
            <p class="status-error" role="alert">@_errorMessage</p>
        }

        @if (_ticket is null)
        {
            @* Step 1 — account details. *@
            <h1>Create the first administrator</h1>
            <p class="lede">
                No administrator exists yet. Set one up now: choose a username and password, then add a
                passkey and an authenticator. All three are required — the passkey and the authenticator
                cannot be skipped.
            </p>

            <EditForm Model="AccountInput" method="post" OnValidSubmit="StartAsync" FormName="setup-account">
                <DataAnnotationsValidator />

                <div class="form-field">
                    <label for="username">Username</label>
                    <InputText id="username" @bind-Value="AccountInput.Username" autocomplete="username"
                               autocapitalize="none" spellcheck="false" autofocus />
                    <ValidationMessage For="@(() => AccountInput.Username)" />
                </div>

                <div class="form-field">
                    <label for="display-name">Display name <span class="optional">(optional)</span></label>
                    <InputText id="display-name" @bind-Value="AccountInput.DisplayName" autocomplete="name" />
                    <ValidationMessage For="@(() => AccountInput.DisplayName)" />
                </div>

                <div class="form-field">
                    <label for="password">Password</label>
                    <InputText id="password" type="password" @bind-Value="AccountInput.Password"
                               autocomplete="new-password" />
                    <ValidationMessage For="@(() => AccountInput.Password)" />
                </div>

                <div class="form-field">
                    <label for="confirm-password">Confirm password</label>
                    <InputText id="confirm-password" type="password" @bind-Value="AccountInput.ConfirmPassword"
                               autocomplete="new-password" />
                    <ValidationMessage For="@(() => AccountInput.ConfirmPassword)" />
                </div>

                <div class="form-actions">
                    <button type="submit" class="button-primary">Continue to passkey</button>
                </div>
            </EditForm>

            <p class="form-footnote">
                Use at least 12 characters. Your operating system's password manager can generate and
                store a strong one for you.
            </p>
        }
        else if (_ticket.Step == SetupStep.Passkey)
        {
            @* Step 2 — passkey registration (WebAuthn attestation). *@
            <h1>Add a passkey</h1>
            <p class="lede">
                A passkey lets you sign in with your fingerprint, face, or device PIN, and it cannot be
                phished. Register one now for <strong>@_ticket.Username</strong>. You can add more, and
                rename this one, later.
            </p>

            <form class="passkey-add" @formname="setup-passkey" method="post" @onsubmit="RegisterPasskeyAsync">
                <AntiforgeryToken />
                <PasskeySubmit Operation="PasskeyOperation.Create" Name="PasskeyInput"
                               CreationOptionsUrl="@AccountRoutes.SetupPasskeyCreationOptions" class="button-primary">
                    Register a passkey
                </PasskeySubmit>
            </form>
        }
        else if (_ticket.Step == SetupStep.Totp)
        {
            @* Step 3 — authenticator (TOTP) enrollment. *@
            <h1>Set up your authenticator</h1>
            <p class="lede">
                Scan this QR code with an authenticator app (or type the key), then enter the six-digit
                code it shows. This is your second factor when you sign in with a password.
            </p>

            <div class="totp-qr">
                @((MarkupString)_qrCodeSvg)
            </div>

            <p class="totp-secret">@_manualEntrySecret</p>

                <div class="form-field">
                    <label for="code">Six-digit code</label>
                    <InputText id="code" @bind-Value="TotpInput.Code" autocomplete="one-time-code"
                               inputmode="numeric" autocapitalize="none" spellcheck="false" autofocus />
                    <ValidationMessage For="@(() => TotpInput.Code)" />

                    <button type="submit" class="button-primary">Confirm and review</button>
                </div>

        }
        else
        {
            @* Step 4 — review and commit. *@
            <h1>Review and finish</h1>
            <p class="lede">
                Everything is ready. Creating the administrator writes the account, your passkey, your
                authenticator, and your recovery codes together, and grants the administrator role.
            </p>

            <dl class="setup-summary">
                <div>
                    <dt>Username</dt>
                    <dd>@_ticket.Username</dd>
                </div>
                <div>
                    <dt>Display name</dt>
                    <dd>@(string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(_ticket.DisplayName) ? "—" : _ticket.DisplayName)</dd>
                </div>
                <div>
                    <dt>Passkey</dt>
                    <dd>Registered</dd>
                </div>
                <div>
                    <dt>Authenticator</dt>
                    <dd>Confirmed</dd>
                </div>

            <form @formname="setup-finish" method="post" @onsubmit="FinishAsync">
                <AntiforgeryToken />

                    <button type="submit" class="button-primary">Create administrator</button>
                </div>
            </form>
        }

        @if (_ticket is not null)
        {
            <form @formname="setup-restart" method="post" @onsubmit="RestartAsync" class="setup-restart">
                <AntiforgeryToken />
                <button type="submit" class="link-button">Start over</button>
            </form>
        }
    </section>
}

@code {
    private SetupTicketProtector _protector = default!;
    private SetupTicket? _ticket;
    private bool _adminExists;
    private bool _completed;
    private string? _completedUsername;
    private IReadOnlyList<string>? _recoveryCodes;
    private string? _errorMessage;

    // Prepared once for the TOTP step so the same QR survives a mistyped-code re-render.
    private string _qrCodeSvg = string.Empty;
    private string _manualEntrySecret = string.Empty;

    [CascadingParameter]
    private HttpContext HttpContext { get; set; } = default!;

    [SupplyParameterFromForm(FormName = "setup-account")]
    private AccountInputModel AccountInput { get; set; } = default!;

    [SupplyParameterFromForm(FormName = "setup-passkey")]
    private PasskeyInputModel PasskeyInput { get; set; } = default!;

    [SupplyParameterFromForm(FormName = "setup-totp")]
    private TotpInputModel TotpInput { get; set; } = default!;

    protected override async Task OnInitializedAsync()
    {
        // BL0008: a form POST binds these itself and may assign null, so defaults live here.
        AccountInput ??= new();
        PasskeyInput ??= new();
        TotpInput ??= new();
        _protector = new SetupTicketProtector(DataProtection);

        // The unlocked gate: if any administrator exists, /setup is gone (§3.6). The authoritative
        // re-check happens under the advisory lock at commit, so a race here is harmless.
        _adminExists = await Bootstrap.AdministratorExistsAsync(HttpContext.RequestAborted);
        if (_adminExists)
        {
            HttpContext.Response.StatusCode = StatusCodes.Status404NotFound;
            return;
        }

        if (HttpContext.Request.Cookies.TryGetValue(SetupCookie.Name, out string? cookie)
            && _protector.TryUnprotect(cookie, out SetupTicket? ticket)
            && ticket is not null
            && !ticket.HasExpired(Clock.UtcNow, SetupCookie.Lifetime))
        {
            _ticket = ticket;
            if (_ticket.Step == SetupStep.Totp && !string.IsNullOrEmpty(_ticket.TotpSecretBase32))
            {
                PrepareTotpDisplay(_ticket);
            }
        }
        else if (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(cookie))
        {
            // Stale, tampered, or from another key: drop it and start clean.
            SetupCookie.Delete(HttpContext.Response);
            _errorMessage = "Your setup session expired. Please start again.";
        }
    }

    private async Task StartAsync()
    {
        if (_adminExists)
        {
            return;
        }

        string username = AccountInput.Username.Trim();
        string? displayName = string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(AccountInput.DisplayName)
            ? null
            : AccountInput.DisplayName.Trim();

        // Best-effort duplicate check; the person UNIQUE constraint and the commit are authoritative.
        if (await UserManager.FindByNameAsync(username) is not null)
        {
            _errorMessage = "That username is already taken. Please choose another.";
            return;
        }

        Guid personIdentifier = IdentifierFactory.Create();

        // Hash immediately so the plaintext is never carried in the ticket. The hasher ignores the
        // user argument (no per-user pepper, §3.2); a throwaway carrier is fine.
        string passwordHash = PasswordHasher.HashPassword(
            new Person { PersonIdentifier = personIdentifier, Username = username },
            AccountInput.Password);

        WriteTicketAndReload(new SetupTicket(
            personIdentifier,
            Clock.UtcNow,
            SetupStep.Passkey,
            username,
            displayName,
            passwordHash,
            Passkey: null,
            TotpSecretBase32: null));
    }

    private async Task RegisterPasskeyAsync()
    {
        if (_adminExists)
        {
            return;
        }

        if (_ticket is null || _ticket.Step != SetupStep.Passkey)
        {
            Navigation.NavigateTo(AccountRoutes.Setup);
            return;
        }

        if (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(PasskeyInput.Error))
        {
            _errorMessage = "That passkey could not be added. Please try again.";
            return;
        }

        if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(PasskeyInput.CredentialJson))
        {
            _errorMessage = "Your browser did not provide a passkey.";
            return;
        }

        PasskeyAttestationResult attestation =
            await SignInManager.PerformPasskeyAttestationAsync(PasskeyInput.CredentialJson);
        if (!attestation.Succeeded || attestation.Passkey is null)
        {
            _errorMessage = "That passkey could not be registered. Please try again.";
            return;
        }

        UserPasskeyInfo info = attestation.Passkey;
        SetupPasskey passkey = new(
            info.CredentialId,
            info.PublicKey,
            (long)info.SignCount,
            info.Transports,
            Name: $"Passkey added {RestaurantClock.Date(Clock.UtcNow)}",
            info.IsUserVerified,
            info.IsBackupEligible,
            info.IsBackedUp);

        // Mint the authenticator secret now so the TOTP step's QR is stable across re-renders.
        string totpSecretBase32 = Base32Text.Encode(Rfc6238Totp.GenerateSecret());

        WriteTicketAndReload(_ticket with
        {
            Step = SetupStep.Totp,
            Passkey = passkey,
            TotpSecretBase32 = totpSecretBase32,
        });
    }

    private Task ConfirmTotpAsync()
    {
        if (_adminExists)
        {
            return Task.CompletedTask;
        }

        if (_ticket is null || _ticket.Step != SetupStep.Totp || string.IsNullOrEmpty(_ticket.TotpSecretBase32))
        {
            Navigation.NavigateTo(AccountRoutes.Setup);
            return Task.CompletedTask;
        }

        if (!Base32Text.TryDecode(_ticket.TotpSecretBase32, out byte[] secret))
        {
            SetupCookie.Delete(HttpContext.Response);
            _ticket = null;
            _errorMessage = "Something went wrong with the setup code. Please start again.";
            return Task.CompletedTask;
        }

        string normalized = (TotpInput.Code ?? string.Empty).Replace(" ", string.Empty).Replace("-", string.Empty);
        if (!Rfc6238Totp.ValidateCode(secret, normalized, Clock.UtcNow))
        {
            // The QR was already prepared in OnInitializedAsync (step is still Totp); it re-renders.
            _errorMessage = "That code did not match. Check your authenticator and try again.";
            return Task.CompletedTask;
        }

        WriteTicketAndReload(_ticket with { Step = SetupStep.Review });
        return Task.CompletedTask;
    }

    private async Task FinishAsync()
    {
        if (_adminExists)
        {
            return;
        }

        if (_ticket is null
            || _ticket.Step != SetupStep.Review
            || _ticket.Passkey is null
            || string.IsNullOrEmpty(_ticket.TotpSecretBase32))
        {
            Navigation.NavigateTo(AccountRoutes.Setup);
            return;
        }

        SetupPasskey stored = _ticket.Passkey;
        UserPasskeyInfo passkey = new(
            stored.CredentialId,
            stored.PublicKey,
            Clock.UtcNow, // placeholder; the bootstrap stamps created_at itself
            (uint)stored.SignatureCounter,
            stored.Transports,
            stored.IsUserVerified,
            stored.IsBackupEligible,
            stored.IsBackedUp,
            attestationObject: [],
            clientDataJson: [])
        {
            Name = stored.Name,
        };

        FirstAdministratorBootstrapResult result = await Bootstrap.CreateFirstAdministratorAsync(
            new NewAdministrator(
                _ticket.PersonIdentifier,
                _ticket.Username,
                _ticket.DisplayName,
                _ticket.PasswordHash,
                _ticket.TotpSecretBase32,
                passkey),
            HttpContext.RequestAborted);

        // Whatever happens next, the wizard is finished with the cookie.
        SetupCookie.Delete(HttpContext.Response);

        if (result.Status == FirstAdministratorBootstrapStatus.AdministratorAlreadyExists)
        {
            // Lost the race (or setup already ran): behave as if /setup is gone.
            _adminExists = true;
            _ticket = null;
            HttpContext.Response.StatusCode = StatusCodes.Status404NotFound;
            return;
        }

        // Created: sign the new administrator in on this response, then show the codes once.
        Person? administrator = await UserManager.FindByIdAsync(_ticket.PersonIdentifier.ToString());
        if (administrator is not null)
        {
            await SignInManager.SignInAsync(administrator, isPersistent: true);
        }

        _completedUsername = _ticket.Username;
        _recoveryCodes = result.RecoveryCodes;
        _completed = true;
        _ticket = null;
    }

    private void RestartAsync()
    {
        SetupCookie.Delete(HttpContext.Response);
        Navigation.NavigateTo(AccountRoutes.Setup);
    }

    // Writes the protected ticket cookie and follows post/redirect/get so a refresh does not re-post
    // the step. NavigateTo during static SSR surfaces as an HTTP redirect carrying the fresh cookie.
    private void WriteTicketAndReload(SetupTicket ticket)
    {
        SetupCookie.Write(HttpContext.Response, _protector.Protect(ticket));
        Navigation.NavigateTo(AccountRoutes.Setup);
    }

    private void PrepareTotpDisplay(SetupTicket ticket)
    {
        string provisioningUri = TotpProvisioningUri.Build(Options.RestaurantName, ticket.Username, ticket.TotpSecretBase32!);
        _qrCodeSvg = TotpQrCode.RenderSvg(provisioningUri);
        _manualEntrySecret = GroupForManualEntry(ticket.TotpSecretBase32!);
    }

    // The active step index (Account=0, Passkey=1, Authenticator=2, Finish=3).
    private int ActiveStepIndex => _ticket is null
        ? 0
        : _ticket.Step switch
        {
            SetupStep.Passkey => 1,
            SetupStep.Totp => 2,
            _ => 3,
        };

    private string StepClass(int index)
        => index == ActiveStepIndex ? "setup-step is-current"
            : index < ActiveStepIndex ? "setup-step is-done"
            : "setup-step";

    /// <summary>Groups the Base32 secret into space-separated blocks of four for easier manual entry.</summary>
    private static string GroupForManualEntry(string base32)
    {
        StringBuilder builder = new(base32.Length + (base32.Length / 4));
        for (int index = 0; index < base32.Length; index++)
        {
            if (index > 0 && index % 4 == 0)
            {
                builder.Append(' ');
            }

            builder.Append(base32[index]);
        }

        return builder.ToString();
    }

    private sealed class AccountInputModel
    {
        [Required(ErrorMessage = "Choose a username.")]
        [StringLength(64, MinimumLength = 3, ErrorMessage = "The username must be 3–64 characters.")]
        public string Username { get; set; } = string.Empty;

        [StringLength(120, ErrorMessage = "That display name is too long.")]
        public string? DisplayName { get; set; }

        [Required(ErrorMessage = "Choose a password.")]
        [StringLength(256, MinimumLength = 12, ErrorMessage = "Use at least 12 characters.")]
        public string Password { get; set; } = string.Empty;

        [Required(ErrorMessage = "Re-enter the password.")]
        [Compare(nameof(Password), ErrorMessage = "The passwords do not match.")]
        public string ConfirmPassword { get; set; } = string.Empty;
    }

    private sealed class TotpInputModel
    {
        [Required(ErrorMessage = "Enter the six-digit code from your authenticator app.")]
        public string Code { get; set; } = string.Empty;
    }
}

   Interactive server, unlike /table/{id}: this page sets no cookie and issues no redirect, so it can
   stay on the circuit, and it remains the standing proof that the whole chain — cookie → claims →
   area policy → AuthorizeRouteView → circuit — is live. Anonymous visitors are sent to /sign-in with

   duplicating any of it here would mean a second surface to keep in step with §6. *@

@code {
    private IReadOnlyList<TableSittingSummary> _sittings = [];
    private bool _loaded;

    [CascadingParameter]
    private Task<AuthenticationState>? AuthenticationStateTask { get; set; }

    protected override async Task OnInitializedAsync()
    {
        // The cascading authentication state is the circuit-safe way to read the principal: there is
        // no HttpContext once the component is interactive, and this works identically during the
        // static prerender pass (AddCascadingAuthenticationState is wired in AddRestaurantIdentity).
        if (AuthenticationStateTask is not null)
        {
            AuthenticationState state = await AuthenticationStateTask;
            if (PersonPrincipal.IdentifierFor(state.User) is { } person)
            {
                _sittings = await Sittings.ListOpenSittingsForPersonAsync(person);
            }
        }

        _loaded = true;
    }
}

@* The guest's own order history, and §6.8's Hide (TECHNICAL_SPECIFICATION §6.8, §11.1).

   §11.1 puts two things on the guest's side of this feature: "history (the guest's **own** past orders at
   this restaurant — cross-member history is never shown)" and "a per-order **Hide** control on closed
   orders, confirmed as irreversible from the guest's account (§6.8)". This is both, and it is a route of
   its own rather than a panel on /table/{id} because a history spans sittings while that page is scoped
   to one — §5.1 is explicit that "the UI scopes to the sitting behind the current /table/{id} route", and
   a list of last month's meals is not part of the sitting somebody is currently eating.

   Static SSR, not an interactive island. The two things this page does are read a list and post a
   confirmed write that then redirects (post/redirect/get, so a refresh cannot re-hide), and neither needs
   a circuit. The live surface next door is interactive because a party total moves while you watch it; a
   settled bill from three weeks ago does not.

   The confirmation is a step, not a dialog. §6.8 requires it to state "plainly that this cannot be undone
   from the guest's account", and a browser confirm() cannot be read, cannot be styled, and does not exist
   without JavaScript — while this page works with none. Tapping Hide navigates to ?hide={order}, which
   renders the warning inline above the row with the only two things to do next: confirm, or go back. *@

<PageTitle>Your order history</PageTitle>

                        <p class="history-order-when">
                            @RestaurantClock.Date(entry.OpenedAt) ·
                            @RestaurantClock.Time(entry.OpenedAt) to @RestaurantClock.Time(entry.ClosedAt)
                        </p>
                    </div>
                    <div class="history-order-total">
                        <span class="history-amount">@Money(entry.PersonTotalAmount)</span>
                        <span class="history-order-count">
                            @entry.LineCount @(entry.LineCount == 1 ? "item" : "items")
                        </span>
                    </div>
                </header>

                @if (Hide == entry.GuestOrderIdentifier)
                {
                    @* §6.8's confirmation, stated the way §6.8 requires. *@
                    <div class="history-confirm" role="alert">
                        <p class="history-confirm-title"><strong>Hide this from your history?</strong></p>
                        <p>
                            It will stop appearing here. <strong>You will not be able to put it back</strong>
                            — there is no undo on your account. If you need it again afterwards you will have
                            to ask a manager, who can restore it.
                        </p>
                        <p class="history-confirm-note">
                            The restaurant's own records are unchanged: what you ordered, what it cost, and
                            what was settled all stay exactly as they are. This only controls whether the
                            order shows up on this page.
                        </p>

                        <form method="post" @formname="hide-order" @onsubmit="HideAsync">
                            <AntiforgeryToken />
                            <input type="hidden" name="@OrderField" value="@entry.GuestOrderIdentifier" />

                            <div class="form-actions">
                                <button type="submit" class="button-primary">
                                    Yes, hide it permanently
                                </button>
                                <a class="button-secondary" href="/table/history">Keep it</a>
                            </div>
                        </form>
                    </div>
                }

                @if (entry.Lines.Count == 0)
                {
                    <p class="history-empty">
                        Nothing was left on this order by the end — every line had been taken off.
                    </p>
                }
                else
                {
                    <ul class="history-lines">
                        @foreach (OrderLineView line in entry.Lines)
                        {
                            <li>
                                <span class="history-line-quantity">@line.Quantity ×</span>
                                <span class="history-line-item">@line.MenuItemName</span>
                                @if (!string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(line.CustomizationNote))
                                {
                                    <span class="history-line-note">“@line.CustomizationNote.Trim()”</span>
                                }

                {
                    <p class="history-order-actions">
                        <a class="history-hide-link" href="@HidePath(entry)">Hide this from my history</a>

            </article>

            The newest @_entries.Count, capped at @HistoryCap. Times are the restaurant's own, as they are
            everywhere here — the footer below says which clock that is.
        </p>

    <p><a href="/table">Back to your tables</a></p>

@code {
    /// <summary>
    /// How far back the list goes. Bounded because this is a phone screen and a regular's history is
    /// unbounded; newest-first because the order somebody is looking for is nearly always the last one.
    /// </summary>
    private const int HistoryCap = 50;

    /// <summary>
    /// The one field the POST handler reads. The order identifier travels in a hidden input rather than
    /// being re-read from the <c>?hide=</c> query string, so the write does not depend on the browser
    /// preserving a query on a form whose action is the current document.
    /// </summary>
    private const string OrderField = "order";

    private IReadOnlyList<PersonOrderHistoryEntry>? _entries;
    private string? _flashMessage;
    private string? _errorMessage;

    [CascadingParameter]
    private HttpContext HttpContext { get; set; } = default!;

    /// <summary>
    /// Which order the confirmation step is open for, if any. A value that names an order not in the list
    /// below — a stale link, or somebody else's identifier — opens no panel and says so.
    /// </summary>
    [SupplyParameterFromQuery]
    private Guid? Hide { get; set; }

    [SupplyParameterFromQuery]
    private string? Done { get; set; }

    protected override async Task OnInitializedAsync()
    {
        await LoadAsync();

        if (HttpMethods.IsGet(HttpContext.Request.Method))
        {
            _flashMessage = FlashFor(Done);

            if (Hide is { } requested && _entries is not null
                && !_entries.Any(entry => entry.GuestOrderIdentifier == requested))
            {
                _errorMessage =
                    "That order is not in your history — it may already be hidden, or the link may be from " +
                    "an older page. Everything you can still see is below.";
            }
        }
    }

    private async Task LoadAsync()
    {
        if (PersonPrincipal.IdentifierFor(HttpContext.User) is not { } person)
        {
            // Only reachable if the cookie expired between the request being authorized and this render.
            _entries = [];
            _errorMessage = "Your session could not be identified. Sign in again to see your history.";
            return;
        }

        _entries = await History.ListVisibleHistoryForPersonAsync(
            person, HistoryCap, HttpContext.RequestAborted);
    }

    /// <summary>
    /// §6.8's owner hide, through the workflow so the change is announced (§9). The service re-checks
    /// everything this page believes — that the order is this person's, that its sitting is closed, that
    /// it is not already hidden — under its own lock, because a page's belief about who owns a row is not
    /// a permission.
    /// </summary>
    private async Task HideAsync()
    {
        if (PersonPrincipal.IdentifierFor(HttpContext.User) is not { } person)
        {
            _errorMessage = "Your session could not be identified. Sign in again and retry.";
            await LoadAsync();
            return;
        }

        IFormCollection form = await HttpContext.Request.ReadFormAsync(HttpContext.RequestAborted);

        // Not a second read of the body: the Blazor endpoint has already parsed the form to find this
        // handler, and HttpRequest caches the parsed collection, so this is the same instance the
        // framework used. Awaiting the cached path rather than touching Request.Form synchronously keeps
        // the cancellation token honoured. Same shape as AdministrationSittings.
        // Read out to string? first: form[key] is a StringValues, and being explicit about the conversion
        // keeps overload resolution on Guid.TryParse(string?, out Guid) rather than leaving it to an
        // implicit conversion to pick between that and the span overload.
        string? postedOrder = form[OrderField];

        if (!Guid.TryParse(postedOrder, out Guid guestOrderIdentifier))
        {
            _errorMessage = "That request did not name an order, so nothing was hidden.";
            await LoadAsync();
            return;
        }

        HideOrderResult result = await Visibility.HideAsync(
            guestOrderIdentifier, person, HttpContext.RequestAborted);

        if (result.Outcome is HideOrderOutcome.Hidden or HideOrderOutcome.AlreadyHidden)
        {
            // Post/redirect/get: a refresh must not re-post. AlreadyHidden redirects too — the order is in
            // the state the person asked for, and telling them it "failed" would be both untrue and
            // alarming about a record they were trying to tidy.
            Navigation.NavigateTo("/table/history?done=hidden");
            return;
        }

        _errorMessage = DescribeRefusal(result.Outcome);
        await LoadAsync();
    }

    /// <summary>
    /// The three refusals, in the guest's words rather than the service's. None of them is reachable from
    /// the markup above — the list only offers Hide on the person's own settled, visible orders — so each
    /// means either a replayed post or a page that has gone stale under somebody, and the sentence says
    /// what to do about that rather than naming an outcome.
    /// </summary>
    private static string DescribeRefusal(HideOrderOutcome outcome) => outcome switch
    {
        HideOrderOutcome.OrderNotFound =>
            "That order no longer exists, so there was nothing to hide.",
        HideOrderOutcome.NotTheOwner =>
            "That is not your order, so it was not hidden. Only your own orders appear on this page.",
        HideOrderOutcome.SittingStillOpen =>
            "That table is still open, so its order is not history yet — you can see it live on your " +
            "table's page. It can be hidden once the counter settles the bill.",
        _ =>
            "Nothing was hidden. Reload the page and try again.",
    };

    private static string? FlashFor(string? done) => done switch
    {
        "hidden" =>
            "Hidden. It is off this page for good — a manager can restore it if you ever need it back.",
        _ => null,
    };

    private static string HidePath(PersonOrderHistoryEntry entry)
        => $"/table/history?hide={entry.GuestOrderIdentifier}";

    private string Money(decimal amount) => MoneyText.Format(amount, Options.CurrencyCode);
}

@attribute [ExcludeFromInteractiveRouting]
@using MyRestaurant.DataAccess.Sittings

@* The table join flow and the member's table surface (TECHNICAL_SPECIFICATION §4.4, §5.1, §11.1).

   Deliberately ANONYMOUS and static SSR. Anonymous because a guest scanning a table's QR for the
   first time has no account yet, and §4.4 requires the grant to be issued *before* the detour through
   sign-in — the whole point of the grant is that it survives that detour. Static SSR because the flow
   writes and clears a cookie and issues redirects, none of which a Blazor circuit can do.

   The four states this page resolves to, in the order §4.4 decides them:

     1. Member  — an authenticated member of this table's open sitting. Members bypass tokens
                  entirely: no query string is consulted, and a deactivated table does not evict
                  anyone (§4.1 stops *new* tokens and display rendering, not a sitting in progress).
     2. Confirm — a non-member holding a live grant, signed in. One button turns the grant into
                  membership.
     3. (redirect) — a non-member holding a live grant, anonymous: off to sign-in with this page as
                  the return URL. The grant cookie is already written, so the trip back needs no token.
     4. Expired — everything else, rendered as a friendly re-scan page at HTTP 200 with no detail
                  about *which* thing failed (§4.4: "no oracle detail"). An unknown table, a
                  deactivated table, a stale token, and a forged grant are indistinguishable here.

   The join itself is a post/redirect/get: the POST consumes the grant, opens or joins the sitting in
   one transaction (§5.1), broadcasts SittingMemberJoined only when a membership row was actually
   inserted (§9), and redirects back here so a refresh cannot re-post.

   The MEMBER stage hosts <TableOrderSurface> as an interactive-server island. Everything §11.1 asks
   for below the join — a basket, a Send that reports per-operation reasons, lines that re-badge when
   the kitchen fulfills them, a party total that moves when someone else orders, the flip to a settled
   bill on SittingClosed — is live, and none of it can happen on a statically rendered page. Splitting
   it this way keeps the cookie work where an HTTP response exists and the live work on a circuit,
   rather than compromising one for the other. The roster moved into the island for the same reason:
   §9 sends SittingMemberJoined to table members, and a statically rendered list cannot hear it. *@

<PageTitle>@PageTitleText</PageTitle>

@if (_stage == JoinStage.Member && _table is not null && _sitting is not null)

        <p class="lede">

@code {
    /// <summary>Which of the §4.4 outcomes this request resolved to. A redirect never reaches a stage.</summary>
    private enum JoinStage
    {
        /// <summary>Friendly re-scan page (§4.4) — the catch-all, and the default before anything is decided.</summary>
        Expired,

        /// <summary>Signed in, holding a live grant, not yet a member: offer the join button.</summary>
        Confirm,

        /// <summary>A member of this table's open sitting: the table surface itself.</summary>
        Member,
    }

    private JoinStage _stage = JoinStage.Expired;
    private RestaurantTableSummary? _table;
    private TableSittingSummary? _sitting;
    private int _openSittingMemberCount;
    private bool _justJoined;

    [Parameter]
    public Guid TableId { get; set; }

    [CascadingParameter]
    private HttpContext HttpContext { get; set; } = default!;

    [SupplyParameterFromQuery(Name = "token")]
    private string? Token { get; set; }

    [SupplyParameterFromQuery(Name = "joined")]
    private string? Joined { get; set; }

    private TimeSpan GrantLifetime => TimeSpan.FromMinutes(Options.TableJoinGrantMinutes);

    private string TablePath => $"/table/{TableId}";

    private string PageTitleText => _stage switch
    {
        JoinStage.Member when _table is not null => _table.Label,
        JoinStage.Confirm when _table is not null => $"Join {_table.Label}",
        _ => "Join a table",
    };

    protected override async Task OnInitializedAsync()
    {
        CancellationToken cancellationToken = HttpContext.RequestAborted;
        bool isGet = HttpMethods.IsGet(HttpContext.Request.Method);

        _table = await TableDirectory.GetTableAsync(TableId, cancellationToken);
        if (_table is null)
        {
            // No oracle: an unknown table reads exactly like a stale code (§4.4).
            _stage = JoinStage.Expired;
            return;
        }

        Guid? personIdentifier = PersonPrincipal.IdentifierFor(HttpContext.User);

        // (1) Members bypass tokens entirely (§4.4) — and a deactivated table does not evict them.
        if (personIdentifier is { } member)
        {
            _sitting = await Sittings.GetOpenSittingForMemberAsync(TableId, member, cancellationToken);
            if (_sitting is not null)
            {
                // The roster, the order, and the totals are the island's job from here — this page
                // stops at "you are a member of this sitting, here is the identifier".
                _stage = JoinStage.Member;
                _justJoined = isGet && string.Equals(Joined, "yes", StringComparison.Ordinal);
                return;
            }
        }

        // (2) A non-member cannot join a table that is out of service (§4.1).
        if (!_table.IsActive)
        {
            _stage = JoinStage.Expired;
            return;
        }

        // (3) A presented token is always validated on a GET, so the §4.3 metric counts every scan —
        // even when a grant is already held. A valid one (re)issues the grant and restarts its clock.
        // The join POST re-posts to this same URL, query string and all; re-validating there would
        // double-count one scan, so the metric stays on the navigation that actually is a scan.
        bool holdsGrant = false;
        if (isGet && !string.IsNullOrEmpty(Token))
        {
            JoinTokenValidationResult validation = await JoinTokens.ValidateAsync(TableId, Token, cancellationToken);
            if (validation == JoinTokenValidationResult.Valid)
            {
                JoinGrantCookie.Write(
                    HttpContext.Response,
                    Grants.Protect(new JoinGrant(TableId, Clock.UtcNow)),
                    GrantLifetime);
                holdsGrant = true;
            }
        }

        // (4) No usable token is not the end: an unconsumed grant from an earlier scan still counts.
        // That is what carries the flow back from sign-in, where the return URL has no token (§4.4).
        holdsGrant = holdsGrant || TryReadUsableGrant();

        if (!holdsGrant)
        {
            _stage = JoinStage.Expired;
            return;
        }

        if (personIdentifier is null)
        {
            // Anonymous with a live grant → sign in (or register) and come straight back here (§4.4).
            Navigation.NavigateTo($"{AccountRoutes.SignIn}?ReturnUrl={Uri.EscapeDataString(TablePath)}");
            return;
        }

        // Purely for the confirmation copy — how full the table already is. Skipped on the join POST,
        // which either redirects or falls to the expired page and never renders that sentence.
        if (isGet)
        {
            TableSittingSummary? openSitting = await Sittings.GetOpenSittingAsync(TableId, cancellationToken);
            _openSittingMemberCount = openSitting?.MemberCount ?? 0;
        }

        _stage = JoinStage.Confirm;
    }

    /// <summary>
    /// Turns the held grant into membership (§4.4, §5.1). Every precondition is re-checked here rather
    /// than trusted from the render that drew the button: a POST is a separate request, and the grant
    /// may have expired, been spent, or never have matched this table at all.
    /// </summary>
    private async Task JoinAsync()
    {
        CancellationToken cancellationToken = HttpContext.RequestAborted;

        if (PersonPrincipal.IdentifierFor(HttpContext.User) is not { } person)
        {
            Navigation.NavigateTo($"{AccountRoutes.SignIn}?ReturnUrl={Uri.EscapeDataString(TablePath)}");
            return;
        }

        if (!TryReadUsableGrant())
        {
            JoinGrantCookie.Delete(HttpContext.Response);
            _stage = JoinStage.Expired;
            return;
        }

        JoinTableResult result = await Membership.JoinTableAsync(TableId, person, cancellationToken);

        // Single-use, whatever the outcome: a spent or refused grant must never be replayable (§4.4).
        JoinGrantCookie.Delete(HttpContext.Response);

        if (result.Outcome == JoinTableOutcome.TableUnavailable)
        {
            _stage = JoinStage.Expired;
            return;
        }

        // After commit, and only when a membership row was really inserted (§9: "fired on: membership
        // insert"). An idempotent re-join writes nothing and so announces nothing.
        if (result.MembershipInserted && result.SittingIdentifier is { } sittingIdentifier)
        {
            Broadcaster.Publish(new SittingMemberJoined(sittingIdentifier));
        }

        Navigation.NavigateTo($"{TablePath}?joined=yes");
    }

    /// <summary>
    /// True when the request carries a grant that is ours, intact, names <b>this</b> table, and has not
    /// aged past <c>TABLE_JOIN_GRANT_MINUTES</c>. The lifetime is judged against the protected
    /// <c>issued_at</c>, not the cookie's own expiry, because only the former is beyond the guest's reach.
    /// </summary>
    private bool TryReadUsableGrant()
        => Grants.TryUnprotect(JoinGrantCookie.Read(HttpContext.Request), out JoinGrant? grant)
            && grant is not null
            && grant.IsUsableFor(TableId, Clock.UtcNow, GrantLifetime);
}

@using System.Globalization
@using MyRestaurant.DataAccess.Menu
@using MyRestaurant.DataAccess.Orders
@using MyRestaurant.DataAccess.Sittings
@using MyRestaurant.Domain.Identifiers
@using MyRestaurant.Domain.LiveUpdates
@using MyRestaurant.Domain.Orders
@using MyRestaurant.WebApplication.Orders
@implements IDisposable
@inject IMenuDirectory MenuDirectory
@inject IOrderReadModel OrderReads
@inject IOrderEventLog EventLog
@inject IOrderWorkflow Workflow
@inject ISittingDirectory Sittings
@inject IDomainEventBroadcaster Broadcaster
@inject IIdentifierFactory Identifiers
@inject RestaurantOptions Options
@inject RestaurantTime RestaurantClock

@* The guest ordering surface (TECHNICAL_SPECIFICATION §6, §7, §9, §11.1).

   An INTERACTIVE ISLAND inside a static-SSR page, which is the one structural decision in this file
   worth reading twice. /table/{id} is [ExcludeFromInteractiveRouting] because the join flow writes the
   grant cookie and issues redirects, and a Blazor circuit can do neither. But everything §11.1 asks for
   below the join — a basket that survives a mis-tap, a Send that reports per-operation reasons, lines
   that re-badge when the kitchen fulfills them, a party total that moves when someone else orders — is
   live. So the page stays static and hosts this component with @@rendermode="InteractiveServer". The
   parent keeps the cookie work; this keeps the circuit.

   It is deliberately given only the two identifiers it needs and re-derives everything else. The person
   comes from the cascading authentication state rather than from a parameter, so the component is
   correct on its own terms and not merely correct because its caller was careful; membership and
   openness are re-read on every pass, which is what makes the §11.1 flip to a settled view happen
   without anyone telling this component that the counter closed the sitting.

   Nothing here enforces §6.5. The transaction does, under the lock, against a menu it re-reads there
   (§6.6). What this surface refuses — an unavailable item, a quantity outside 1–100, a tick on a line
   that is no longer the guest's to remove — it refuses only so the answer arrives at the moment of the
   tap instead of after a round trip. *@

@if (!_loaded)
{
    <p class="lede">Loading your table…</p>
}
else if (_person is null)
{
    @* Only reachable if the cookie expired between the page render and the circuit starting. *@
    <p class="status-error" role="alert">
        Your session has ended. Please <a href="@AccountRoutes.SignIn">sign in</a> again to see your order.
    </p>
}
else
{
    <h2 class="table-heading">Who is here</h2>

    @if (_sitting is not null)
    {
        <p class="lede">
            Open since @RestaurantClock.Time(_sitting.OpenedAt) —
            @_roster.Count @(_roster.Count == 1 ? "person" : "people") at the table.

    <ul class="table-roster">
        @foreach (SittingMemberSummary member in _roster)

            <li @key="member.PersonIdentifier">

                    <span class="chip">you</span>
                }
                <span class="table-roster-joined">joined @RestaurantClock.Time(member.JoinedAt)</span>
            </li>

    </ul>

    <hr class="table-rule" />

    @if (_sitting is null)

            What was ordered is below, and stays on <a href="/table/history">your order history</a>.

    else
    {
        <h2 class="table-heading">Your order</h2>

        @if (_sendStatus is { } sendStatus)

        @if (_rejection is { Count: > 0 })
        {

               nothing at all was written — not that "some items failed". *@
            <div class="status-error" role="alert">
                <p class="order-reject-lede">
                    <strong>Nothing was sent.</strong> A send is accepted or refused as a whole, so your

        @* ---- staging area (§11.1) ------------------------------------------------------------ *@
        <div class="order-picker">
            <div class="form-field">
                <label for="order-picker-item">Item</label>
                <select id="order-picker-item" @bind="_pickedMenuItemId">
                    <option value="">Choose something…</option>
                    @foreach (MenuItemSummary item in _menu)

                            @item.Name — @Money(item.PriceAmount)@(item.IsActive ? string.Empty : " (currently unavailable)")

                <label for="order-picker-note">Anything to note? <span class="optional">(optional)</span></label>
                <input id="order-picker-note" type="text" maxlength="200" autocomplete="off"
                       placeholder="No onions, extra hot…" @bind="_pickedNote" />

                        }

                               re-validates server-side regardless". Marked, not silently dropped. *@

                                       min="@OrderStaging.MinimumQuantity" max="@OrderStaging.MaximumQuantity" step="1"
                                       value="@staged.Quantity"

                            </label>

                                    @onclick="() => Unstage(staged.StagingIdentifier)">

                            </button>

        }

        <div class="form-actions order-send">
            <button type="button" class="button-primary" disabled="@(_staging.IsEmpty || _sending)"
                    @onclick="SendAsync">
                @(_sending ? "Sending…" : SendLabel)

            @if (!_staging.IsEmpty && StagedTotal > 0m)
            {

            }

    }

    @* ---- the committed living order (§11.1) ---------------------------------------------------- *@
    <h3 class="order-subheading">@(_sitting is null ? "What you ordered" : "Sent to the kitchen")</h3>

    @if (_myLines.Count == 0)
    {

    @* ---- totals and the rest of the party (§11.1) ---------------------------------------------- *@
    @* A <dl> with <div> groupings — dt/dd outside a definition list is invalid HTML5, and the div
       wrappers are what .order-totals lays out. The same shape .account-facts already uses. *@
    <dl class="order-totals">

@code {
    /// <summary>One refused operation, already turned into two readable halves for the panel (§6.5.9).</summary>
    private sealed record RejectedOperation(string What, string Reason);

    private readonly OrderStaging _staging = new();

    // Captured once, so nothing ever touches _lifetime.Token after Dispose has run — the same shape
    // TableDisplay uses for its refresh loop.
    private readonly CancellationTokenSource _lifetime = new();
    private CancellationToken _stopping;
    private IDisposable? _subscription;
    private bool _disposed;

    private Guid? _person;
    private bool _loaded;

    private IReadOnlyList<MenuItemSummary> _menu = [];
    private Dictionary<Guid, MenuItemSummary> _menuById = new();
    private IReadOnlyList<SittingMemberSummary> _roster = [];
    private TableSittingSummary? _sitting;
    private Guid? _myOrderIdentifier;
    private IReadOnlyList<NarratedOrderLine> _myLines = [];
    private IReadOnlyList<SittingBillEntry> _bill = [];
    private Dictionary<Guid, IReadOnlyList<OrderLineView>> _partyLinesByOrder = new();

    private string _pickedMenuItemId = string.Empty;
    private int _pickedQuantity = OrderStaging.MinimumQuantity;
    private string _pickedNote = string.Empty;

    private string? _stagingNotice;
    private string? _sendStatus;
    private string? _pruneNotice;
    private IReadOnlyList<RejectedOperation>? _rejection;
    private bool _sending;

    /// <summary>The table this surface belongs to — used to re-check membership, never trusted for scoping a read.</summary>
    [Parameter]
    [EditorRequired]
    public Guid TableId { get; set; }

    /// <summary>
    /// The sitting the parent resolved. Every query is scoped by this rather than by the table, so a
    /// sitting that closes and is followed by a new one on the same table does not silently swap the
    /// order under the reader's feet — it flips to the settled view, which is what §11.1 asks for.
    /// </summary>
    [Parameter]
    [EditorRequired]
    public Guid SittingId { get; set; }

    [CascadingParameter]
    private Task<AuthenticationState>? AuthenticationStateTask { get; set; }

    /// <summary>
    /// The signed-in person, for the render tree. Every branch that reads it sits behind an
    /// <c>_person is null</c> guard; the fallback exists so the property is total rather than relying on
    /// a pattern variable's definite assignment surviving Razor's generated control flow.
    /// </summary>
    private Guid Person => _person ?? Guid.Empty;

    private IReadOnlyList<SittingBillEntry> OtherPeople
        => _bill.Where(entry => entry.PersonIdentifier != _person).ToArray();

    private decimal MyTotal
        => _bill.FirstOrDefault(entry => entry.PersonIdentifier == _person)?.PersonTotalAmount ?? 0m;

    private decimal TableTotal => _bill.Sum(entry => entry.PersonTotalAmount);

    private decimal StagedTotal => _staging.Lines.Sum(StagedLineTotal);

    private string SendLabel
    {
        get
        {
            int count = _staging.OperationCount;
            return count == 0 ? "Send to the kitchen" : $"Send {count} change{(count == 1 ? string.Empty : "s")}";
        }
    }

    protected override async Task OnInitializedAsync()
    {
        _stopping = _lifetime.Token;

        if (AuthenticationStateTask is not null)
        {
            AuthenticationState state = await AuthenticationStateTask;
            _person = PersonPrincipal.IdentifierFor(state.User);
        }

        if (_person is null)
        {
            _loaded = true;
            return;
        }

        await LoadMenuAsync();
        await LoadAsync();
        _loaded = true;
    }

    protected override void OnAfterRender(bool firstRender)
    {
        if (!firstRender || _person is null)
        {
            return;
        }

        // Only on the circuit: OnAfterRender does not run during prerendering, so the subscription is
        // never created for a render that is about to be thrown away.
        _subscription = Broadcaster.Subscribe(OnDomainNotification);
    }

    /// <summary>
    /// Everything the surface shows, re-read in one pass. Scoped by <see cref="SittingId"/> throughout;
    /// the only query keyed by the table is the membership/openness check, and its answer is discarded
    /// unless it names <em>this</em> sitting.
    /// </summary>
    private async Task LoadAsync()
    {
        if (_person is not { } person)
        {
            return;
        }

        TableSittingSummary? openSitting = await Sittings
            .GetOpenSittingForMemberAsync(TableId, person, _stopping);

        _sitting = openSitting is not null && openSitting.SittingIdentifier == SittingId ? openSitting : null;

        _roster = await Sittings.ListMembersAsync(SittingId, _stopping);

        _myOrderIdentifier = await OrderReads.FindLivingOrderAsync(SittingId, person, _stopping);
        _myLines = _myOrderIdentifier is { } orderIdentifier
            ? OrderNarrative.FromEvents(await EventLog.ReadEventsAsync(orderIdentifier, _stopping))
            : [];

        _bill = await OrderReads.ListSittingBillAsync(SittingId, _stopping);

        // One read for the whole sitting, grouped once, rather than a query per person in the render
        // loop below: §11.1 shows a row for everyone at the table, and a round trip inside that loop
        // would turn a six-person table into six extra queries on every notification.
        IReadOnlyList<OrderLineView> partyLines = await OrderReads.ListLinesForSittingAsync(SittingId, _stopping);
        _partyLinesByOrder = partyLines
            .GroupBy(line => line.GuestOrderIdentifier)
            .ToDictionary(
                group => group.Key,
                group => (IReadOnlyList<OrderLineView>)group.ToArray());

        // A tick that has gone stale — the kitchen fulfilled the line, or staff took it off — would
        // sink every subsequent send, because §6.5.9 refuses the whole event on one bad operation.
        // Drop those marks and say so, rather than letting the guest press Send into a wall.
        _pruneNotice = null;
        int dropped = _staging.PruneRemovals(_myLines
            .Where(line => line.GuestMayRemove(person))
            .Select(line => line.OrderLineIdentifier));

        if (dropped > 0)
        {
            _pruneNotice = dropped == 1
                ? "One line you had marked to remove is no longer yours to remove — it has been unticked."
                : $"{dropped} lines you had marked to remove are no longer yours to remove — they have been unticked.";
        }
    }

    private async Task LoadMenuAsync()
    {
        _menu = await MenuDirectory.ListAsync(_stopping);
        _menuById = _menu.ToDictionary(item => item.MenuItemIdentifier);
    }

    private void StageItem()
    {
        _stagingNotice = null;

        if (!Guid.TryParse(_pickedMenuItemId, out Guid menuItemIdentifier)
            || MenuItem(menuItemIdentifier) is not { } menuItem)
        {
            _stagingNotice = "Choose something from the menu first.";
            return;
        }

        StagingResult result = _staging.Stage(menuItem, _pickedQuantity, _pickedNote);
        if (!result.Accepted)
        {
            _stagingNotice = result.Reason;
            return;
        }

        // A cleared picker is the signal that the tap landed; the basket below is the receipt.
        _pickedMenuItemId = string.Empty;
        _pickedQuantity = OrderStaging.MinimumQuantity;
        _pickedNote = string.Empty;
        _sendStatus = null;
        _rejection = null;
    }

    private void Unstage(Guid stagingIdentifier)
    {
        _staging.Unstage(stagingIdentifier);
        _stagingNotice = null;
    }

    private void ChangeStagedQuantity(Guid stagingIdentifier, ChangeEventArgs args)
    {
        if (!int.TryParse(
                args.Value?.ToString(),
                NumberStyles.Integer,
                CultureInfo.InvariantCulture,
                out int quantity))
        {
            _stagingNotice = $"Choose a quantity between {OrderStaging.MinimumQuantity} and {OrderStaging.MaximumQuantity}.";
            return;
        }

        StagingResult result = _staging.SetQuantity(stagingIdentifier, quantity);
        _stagingNotice = result.Accepted ? null : result.Reason;
    }

    private void ToggleRemoval(NarratedOrderLine line, ChangeEventArgs args)
    {
        bool marked = args.Value is bool value && value;

        _staging.SetMarkedForRemoval(
            line.OrderLineIdentifier,
            $"{line.Quantity} × {MenuItemName(line.MenuItemIdentifier)}",
            marked);

        _sendStatus = null;
        _rejection = null;
    }

    /// <summary>
    /// §11.1's Send: one <c>guest_submission</c> owning every staged add and every ticked removal,
    /// through <see cref="IOrderWorkflow"/> so the commit is both counted (§12) and broadcast (§9). The
    /// basket is cleared only on an accepted event — a refusal leaves it exactly as it was, because
    /// §6.5.9 wrote nothing and the guest is being asked to restage, not to retype.
    /// </summary>
    private async Task SendAsync()
    {
        if (_person is not { } person || _staging.IsEmpty || _sending)
        {
            return;
        }

        _sending = true;
        _sendStatus = null;
        _rejection = null;
        _stagingNotice = null;

        try
        {
            StagedBatch batch = _staging.Build(Identifiers);

            AppendOrderEventResult result = await Workflow
                .SubmitGuestBatchAsync(SittingId, person, batch.Operations, _stopping);

            if (result.IsAppended)
            {
                _sendStatus = DescribeAcceptedSend(result.LinesAdded, result.LinesRemoved);
                _staging.Clear();
            }
            else
            {
                _rejection = DescribeRejection(result, batch);
            }

            await LoadAsync();
        }
        catch (OperationCanceledException)
        {
            // The circuit went away mid-send. The transaction either committed or did not; either way
            // there is no longer anyone to tell.
        }
        finally
        {
            _sending = false;
        }
    }

    private static string DescribeAcceptedSend(int added, int removed)
    {
        if (added > 0 && removed > 0)
        {
            return $"Sent — {added} item{Plural(added)} added and {removed} taken off. The kitchen has been told.";
        }

        if (added > 0)
        {
            return $"Sent — {added} item{Plural(added)} on the way. The kitchen has been told.";
        }

        return $"Sent — {removed} item{Plural(removed)} taken off. The kitchen has been told.";
    }

    private static string Plural(int count) => count == 1 ? string.Empty : "s";

    /// <summary>
    /// Turns a refusal into sentences a guest can act on. <see cref="OrderMutationError.OperationIndex"/>
    /// indexes the operation list that was sent, and <see cref="StagedBatch.Descriptions"/> was built in
    /// exactly that order — which is why the batch is kept rather than rebuilt.
    /// </summary>
    private static IReadOnlyList<RejectedOperation> DescribeRejection(
        AppendOrderEventResult result,
        StagedBatch batch)
    {
        if (result.Outcome is AppendOrderEventOutcome.SittingNotFound or AppendOrderEventOutcome.OrderNotFound)
        {
            return [new RejectedOperation("This table", "It is no longer taking orders. Please speak to the counter.")];
        }

        List<RejectedOperation> problems = [];

        foreach (OrderMutationError error in result.Errors)
        {
            string what = error.OperationIndex >= 0 && error.OperationIndex < batch.Descriptions.Count
                ? batch.Descriptions[error.OperationIndex]
                : "This send";

            problems.Add(new RejectedOperation(what, error.Reason));
        }

        if (problems.Count == 0)
        {
            problems.Add(new RejectedOperation("This send", "It was refused. Please try again."));
        }

        return problems;
    }

    /// <summary>
    /// §9 says which notifications a table member re-queries on. All four that can change what is on
    /// this screen are handled with one re-read: the queries are small, scoped to one sitting, and a
    /// restaurant table is not a hot path. <c>MenuChanged</c> additionally re-reads the menu, which is
    /// how a staged item picks up its "currently unavailable" mark (§7).
    /// </summary>
    private void OnDomainNotification(DomainNotification notification)
    {
        bool concernsThisTable = notification switch
        {
            OrderLinesChanged changed => changed.SittingIdentifier == SittingId,
            LineFulfillmentChanged changed => changed.SittingIdentifier == SittingId,
            SittingMemberJoined joined => joined.SittingIdentifier == SittingId,
            SittingClosed closed => closed.SittingIdentifier == SittingId,
            MenuChanged => true,
            _ => false,
        };

        if (!concernsThisTable)
        {
            return;
        }

        bool menuChanged = notification is MenuChanged;

        _ = InvokeAsync(async () =>
        {
            try
            {
                if (menuChanged)
                {
                    await LoadMenuAsync();
                }

                await LoadAsync();
                StateHasChanged();
            }
            catch (OperationCanceledException)
            {
                // Disposed between the broadcast and the query; nothing to update.
            }
            catch (ObjectDisposedException)
            {
                // Same, one layer down.
            }
        });
    }

    private MenuItemSummary? MenuItem(Guid menuItemIdentifier)
        => _menuById.TryGetValue(menuItemIdentifier, out MenuItemSummary? item) ? item : null;

    /// <summary>
    /// One other person's lines, out of the single sitting-wide read <see cref="LoadAsync"/> already
    /// did. §11.1 shows the rest of the table as names and their items, and this is the second half of
    /// that: <see cref="_bill"/> supplies the name and the total, this supplies the items underneath.
    /// An order with nothing on it — someone who joined and has not sent yet — is absent from the
    /// grouping rather than present and empty, so the empty list is the normal answer, not an error.
    /// </summary>
    private IReadOnlyList<OrderLineView> LinesFor(Guid guestOrderIdentifier)
        => _partyLinesByOrder.TryGetValue(guestOrderIdentifier, out IReadOnlyList<OrderLineView>? lines)
            ? lines
            : [];

    /// <summary>
    /// The item's <em>current</em> name, which is what <c>order_current_line</c> joins too (§8.3), so a
    /// rename reads the same here as on the counter's bill.
    /// </summary>
    private string MenuItemName(Guid menuItemIdentifier) => MenuItem(menuItemIdentifier)?.Name ?? "Item";

    /// <summary>
    /// A staged line's extended price at the price the menu holds <em>now</em> — never a price captured
    /// when it was staged. §6.5.4 prices the line inside the send transaction, so this is the only
    /// figure that can honestly be shown before it.
    /// </summary>
    private decimal StagedLineTotal(StagedOrderLine staged)
        => (MenuItem(staged.MenuItemIdentifier)?.PriceAmount ?? 0m) * staged.Quantity;

    private string Money(decimal amount) => MoneyText.Format(amount, Options.CurrencyCode);

    private static string DescribeRole(OrderActorRole role) => role switch
    {
        OrderActorRole.Guest => "a guest",
        OrderActorRole.Kitchen => "the kitchen",
        OrderActorRole.Counter => "the counter",
        OrderActorRole.Administrator => "an administrator",
        _ => "staff",
    };

    private static string ActorText(OrderActorRole? role, Guid? actor, Guid person)
        => actor is { } actorIdentifier && actorIdentifier == person
            ? "you"
            : DescribeRole(role ?? OrderActorRole.Counter);

    public void Dispose()
    {
        if (_disposed)
        {
            return;
        }

        _disposed = true;
        _subscription?.Dispose();
        _lifetime.Cancel();
        _lifetime.Dispose();
    }
}

@* Top-level router. AuthorizeRouteView enforces [Authorize] on interactive pages: an anonymous
   visitor is sent to the sign-in page with the destination preserved, while an authenticated
   principal that fails an area policy (§3.7) sees the denial where they stand. The cascading
   authentication state comes from AddCascadingAuthenticationState (wired in AddRestaurantIdentity),
   so this works in both static SSR and interactive-server rendering. Static-SSR pages carrying
   [Authorize] are additionally enforced by endpoint authorization on the server. *@
<Router AppAssembly="typeof(Program).Assembly">
    <Found Context="routeData">
        <AuthorizeRouteView RouteData="routeData" DefaultLayout="typeof(MainLayout)">
            <NotAuthorized>
                @if (context.User.Identity?.IsAuthenticated == true)
                {
                    <section class="panel">
                        <p class="eyebrow">Access denied</p>
                        <h1>You do not have access to this area</h1>
                        <p class="lede">
                            You are signed in as <strong>@context.User.Identity?.Name</strong>, but this
                            area requires a role your account does not hold.
                        </p>
                        <p><a href="/">Back to the home page</a></p>
                    </section>
                }
                else
                {
                    <RedirectToSignIn />
                }
            </NotAuthorized>
        </AuthorizeRouteView>
        <FocusOnNavigate RouteData="routeData" Selector="h1" />
    </Found>
</Router>

using System.Globalization;

namespace MyRestaurant.WebApplication.Configuration;

/// <summary>
/// The complete environment-only configuration (TECHNICAL_SPECIFICATION §13; REQUIREMENTS §8:
/// "environment variables only"). Bound once at startup from the flat, long-named,
/// prefixed variables, then <see cref="Validate"/> is run before HTTP is bound so the process
/// fails fast on invalid security-relevant configuration (§13, §3.2 floor guard).
/// </summary>
public sealed class RestaurantOptions
{
    // Argon2 floor guard (TECHNICAL_SPECIFICATION §3.2). Below any of these the process must not start.
    public const int MinimumArgon2MemoryKibibytes = 19456;
    public const int MinimumArgon2Iterations = 2;
    public const int MinimumArgon2Parallelism = 1;

    // Token/grant/pairing lower bounds (§13: "rotation/grant/pairing values ≥ 10 s / ≥ 1 min / ≥ 1 min").
    public const int MinimumTableJoinTokenRotationSeconds = 10;
    public const int MinimumTableJoinGrantMinutes = 1;
    public const int MinimumTableDisplayPairingCodeMinutes = 1;

    /// <summary>
    /// The default trusted WebAuthn origin patterns (TECHNICAL_SPECIFICATION §3.3, ADR-0005). Cloudflare
    /// Quick Tunnels hand out a random <c>*.trycloudflare.com</c> hostname per run, so trusting that
    /// wildcard lets passkeys work in a quick-tunnel demo without knowing the URL at startup. This gates
    /// only WebAuthn relying-party derivation; it is deliberately not a general CORS allowance.
    /// </summary>
    public static readonly IReadOnlyList<string> DefaultTrustedOriginPatterns = ["https://*.trycloudflare.com"];

    /// <summary>Canonical value of <c>RESTAURANT_CLOCK_FORMAT</c> for <c>3:04 PM</c>.</summary>
    public const string TwelveHourClockFormat = "12-hour";

    /// <summary>Canonical value of <c>RESTAURANT_CLOCK_FORMAT</c> for <c>15:04</c>.</summary>
    public const string TwentyFourHourClockFormat = "24-hour";

    /// <summary>
    /// The default clock format (§13). Twelve-hour, matching the other US-shaped defaults on this
    /// type (<c>America/New_York</c>, <c>USD</c>) — and, unlike them, a choice that had to be made
    /// explicitly rather than inherited: before this it came from whatever culture the container image
    /// happened to carry, which is to say from nobody (F-36).
    /// </summary>
    public const string DefaultClockFormat = TwelveHourClockFormat;

    /// <summary>Everything accepted as "twelve-hour", lower-cased. Spelling should not be a trap.</summary>
    private static readonly HashSet<string> TwelveHourSpellings =
        new(StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase) { "12", "12h", "12-hour", "12 hour", "12hour" };

    /// <summary>Everything accepted as "twenty-four-hour", lower-cased.</summary>
    private static readonly HashSet<string> TwentyFourHourSpellings =
        new(StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase) { "24", "24h", "24-hour", "24 hour", "24hour" };

    public required string RestaurantName { get; init; }
    public required string PublicOrigin { get; init; }

    /// <summary>
    /// Additional browser origins that may act as the WebAuthn relying party, as wildcard patterns
    /// (<c>RESTAURANT_TRUSTED_ORIGIN_PATTERNS</c>; §3.3, ADR-0005). The configured <see cref="PublicOrigin"/>
    /// and loopback (in development) are always trusted; these extend that set so a Cloudflare quick
    /// tunnel's per-run <c>*.trycloudflare.com</c> host works without being known at startup. Defaults to
    /// <see cref="DefaultTrustedOriginPatterns"/>; not required so existing constructions keep the default.
    /// </summary>
    public IReadOnlyList<string> TrustedOriginPatterns { get; init; } = DefaultTrustedOriginPatterns;

    public required string TimeZoneId { get; init; }

    /// <summary>
    /// Whether times render as <c>3:04 PM</c> or <c>15:04</c> (<c>RESTAURANT_CLOCK_FORMAT</c>, §13).
    /// Not <c>required</c>, so a construction that predates it keeps the documented default; the whole
    /// point of the setting is that this decision belongs to the restaurant rather than to the image.
    /// </summary>
    public string ClockFormat { get; init; } = DefaultClockFormat;

    public required string CurrencyCode { get; init; }
    public required string DatabaseConnectionString { get; init; }
    public required string DataProtectionKeysDirectory { get; init; }
    public required int KitchenSubmissionReminderSeconds { get; init; }
    public required int TableJoinTokenRotationSeconds { get; init; }
    public required int TableJoinGrantMinutes { get; init; }
    public required int TableDisplayPairingCodeMinutes { get; init; }
    public required int Argon2MemoryKibibytes { get; init; }
    public required int Argon2Iterations { get; init; }
    public required int Argon2Parallelism { get; init; }
    public required int Argon2MaxConcurrentHashes { get; init; }

    public static RestaurantOptions FromConfiguration(IConfiguration configuration)
    {
        ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull(configuration);

        return new RestaurantOptions
        {
            RestaurantName = ReadString(configuration, "RESTAURANT_NAME", "My Restaurant"),
            PublicOrigin = ReadString(configuration, "RESTAURANT_PUBLIC_ORIGIN", "https://localhost:8443"),
            TrustedOriginPatterns = ReadOriginPatterns(configuration, "RESTAURANT_TRUSTED_ORIGIN_PATTERNS", DefaultTrustedOriginPatterns),
            TimeZoneId = ReadString(configuration, "RESTAURANT_TIME_ZONE", "America/New_York"),
            ClockFormat = ReadString(configuration, "RESTAURANT_CLOCK_FORMAT", DefaultClockFormat),
            CurrencyCode = ReadString(configuration, "RESTAURANT_CURRENCY_CODE", "USD"),
            DatabaseConnectionString = ReadString(
                configuration,
                "RESTAURANT_DATABASE_CONNECTION_STRING",
                "Host=localhost;Port=5432;Database=myrestaurant;Username=myrestaurant;Password=myrestaurant"),
            DataProtectionKeysDirectory = ReadString(configuration, "DATA_PROTECTION_KEYS_DIRECTORY", "/var/lib/myrestaurant/dataprotection"),
            KitchenSubmissionReminderSeconds = ReadInt(configuration, "KITCHEN_SUBMISSION_REMINDER_SECONDS", 60),
            TableJoinTokenRotationSeconds = ReadInt(configuration, "TABLE_JOIN_TOKEN_ROTATION_SECONDS", 60),
            TableJoinGrantMinutes = ReadInt(configuration, "TABLE_JOIN_GRANT_MINUTES", 10),
            TableDisplayPairingCodeMinutes = ReadInt(configuration, "TABLE_DISPLAY_PAIRING_CODE_MINUTES", 10),
            Argon2MemoryKibibytes = ReadInt(configuration, "ARGON2_MEMORY_KIBIBYTES", 65536),
            Argon2Iterations = ReadInt(configuration, "ARGON2_ITERATIONS", 3),
            Argon2Parallelism = ReadInt(configuration, "ARGON2_PARALLELISM", 1),
            Argon2MaxConcurrentHashes = ReadInt(configuration, "ARGON2_MAX_CONCURRENT_HASHES", 4),
        };
    }

    /// <summary>Returns a human-readable reason for every invalid setting; empty means valid.</summary>
    public IReadOnlyList<string> Validate()
    {
        List<string> errors = [];

        if (string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(DatabaseConnectionString))
        {
            errors.Add("RESTAURANT_DATABASE_CONNECTION_STRING must be set.");
        }

        if (!Uri.TryCreate(PublicOrigin, UriKind.Absolute, out Uri? origin)
            || !string.Equals(origin.Scheme, Uri.UriSchemeHttps, StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase))
        {
            errors.Add($"RESTAURANT_PUBLIC_ORIGIN must be an absolute https URL (was '{PublicOrigin}').");
        }

        if (!TryResolveTimeZone(TimeZoneId))
        {
            errors.Add($"RESTAURANT_TIME_ZONE '{TimeZoneId}' is not a resolvable time zone on this host.");
        }

        if (!IsKnownClockFormat(ClockFormat))
        {
            errors.Add(
                $"RESTAURANT_CLOCK_FORMAT must be '{TwelveHourClockFormat}' or '{TwentyFourHourClockFormat}' (was '{ClockFormat}').");
        }

        if (CurrencyCode.Length != 3 || !CurrencyCode.All(char.IsAsciiLetter))
        {
            errors.Add($"RESTAURANT_CURRENCY_CODE must be a 3-letter ISO 4217 code (was '{CurrencyCode}').");
        }

        if (Argon2MemoryKibibytes < MinimumArgon2MemoryKibibytes)
        {
            errors.Add($"ARGON2_MEMORY_KIBIBYTES must be at least {MinimumArgon2MemoryKibibytes} (was {Argon2MemoryKibibytes}).");
        }

        if (Argon2Iterations < MinimumArgon2Iterations)
        {
            errors.Add($"ARGON2_ITERATIONS must be at least {MinimumArgon2Iterations} (was {Argon2Iterations}).");
        }

        if (Argon2Parallelism < MinimumArgon2Parallelism)
        {
            errors.Add($"ARGON2_PARALLELISM must be at least {MinimumArgon2Parallelism} (was {Argon2Parallelism}).");
        }

        if (Argon2MaxConcurrentHashes < 1)
        {
            errors.Add($"ARGON2_MAX_CONCURRENT_HASHES must be at least 1 (was {Argon2MaxConcurrentHashes}).");
        }

        if (TableJoinTokenRotationSeconds < MinimumTableJoinTokenRotationSeconds)
        {
            errors.Add($"TABLE_JOIN_TOKEN_ROTATION_SECONDS must be at least {MinimumTableJoinTokenRotationSeconds} (was {TableJoinTokenRotationSeconds}).");
        }

        if (TableJoinGrantMinutes < MinimumTableJoinGrantMinutes)
        {
            errors.Add($"TABLE_JOIN_GRANT_MINUTES must be at least {MinimumTableJoinGrantMinutes} (was {TableJoinGrantMinutes}).");
        }

        if (TableDisplayPairingCodeMinutes < MinimumTableDisplayPairingCodeMinutes)
        {
            errors.Add($"TABLE_DISPLAY_PAIRING_CODE_MINUTES must be at least {MinimumTableDisplayPairingCodeMinutes} (was {TableDisplayPairingCodeMinutes}).");
        }

        if (KitchenSubmissionReminderSeconds < 1)
        {
            errors.Add($"KITCHEN_SUBMISSION_REMINDER_SECONDS must be at least 1 (was {KitchenSubmissionReminderSeconds}).");
        }

        foreach (string pattern in TrustedOriginPatterns)
        {
            if (!IsValidOriginPattern(pattern))
            {
                errors.Add($"RESTAURANT_TRUSTED_ORIGIN_PATTERNS entry '{pattern}' must be an https origin like 'https://*.trycloudflare.com' (scheme://host, optional leading '*.' wildcard label, no path or port).");
            }
        }

        return errors;
    }

    /// <summary>
    /// The host of the configured public origin (§3.3). As of ADR-0005 the WebAuthn relying-party ID
    /// is derived <em>per request</em> from the request host (so a quick tunnel's per-run hostname
    /// works), not pinned to this value; this remains the canonical configured host — used for QR join
    /// URLs (ADR-0009) and as the fallback host presented by <see cref="Identity.PublicOriginMiddleware"/>.
    /// </summary>
    public string ResolveWebAuthnRelyingPartyId() => new Uri(PublicOrigin).Host;

    /// <summary>
    /// The configured display time zone (validated at startup). Every instant the application renders
    /// goes through this zone — see <see cref="Time.RestaurantTime"/>, which is the only caller and the
    /// only place allowed to turn a stored UTC instant into text (§8.1).
    /// </summary>
    public TimeZoneInfo ResolveTimeZone() => TimeZoneInfo.FindSystemTimeZoneById(TimeZoneId);

    /// <summary>
    /// The <see cref="ClockFormat"/> decision as a boolean. An unrecognized value reads as twelve-hour
    /// (the default), but never silently: <see cref="Validate"/> has already refused to start.
    /// </summary>
    public bool UsesTwelveHourClock => !TwentyFourHourSpellings.Contains(ClockFormat.Trim());

    private static bool IsKnownClockFormat(string clockFormat)
    {
        string value = clockFormat.Trim();
        return TwelveHourSpellings.Contains(value) || TwentyFourHourSpellings.Contains(value);
    }

    private static bool TryResolveTimeZone(string timeZoneId)
    {
        try
        {
            _ = TimeZoneInfo.FindSystemTimeZoneById(timeZoneId);
            return true;
        }
        catch (Exception exception) when (exception is TimeZoneNotFoundException or InvalidTimeZoneException)
        {
            return false;
        }
    }

    private static string ReadString(IConfiguration configuration, string key, string fallback)
    {
        string? value = configuration[key];
        return string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(value) ? fallback : value;
    }

    private static int ReadInt(IConfiguration configuration, string key, int fallback)
        => int.TryParse(configuration[key], NumberStyles.Integer, CultureInfo.InvariantCulture, out int value)
            ? value
            : fallback;

    /// <summary>
    /// Reads a comma/space/newline-separated list of origin patterns, trimming empties; returns the
    /// supplied default when the variable is unset or contains no non-empty entries.
    /// </summary>
    private static IReadOnlyList<string> ReadOriginPatterns(
        IConfiguration configuration,
        string key,
        IReadOnlyList<string> fallback)
    {
        string? raw = configuration[key];
        if (string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(raw))
        {
            return fallback;
        }

        char[] separators = new[] { ',', ' ', '\t', '\n', '\r' };
        string[] parts = raw.Split(separators, StringSplitOptions.RemoveEmptyEntries | StringSplitOptions.TrimEntries);
        return parts.Length == 0 ? fallback : parts;
    }

    /// <summary>
    /// A trusted-origin pattern is <c>scheme://host</c> with an https scheme, a non-empty host that
    /// may begin with a single <c>*.</c> wildcard label, and no path, query, fragment, userinfo, or
    /// port. This matches the runtime matcher in <see cref="Identity.WebAuthnOriginPolicy"/>.
    /// </summary>
    private static bool IsValidOriginPattern(string pattern)
    {
        if (string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(pattern))
        {
            return false;
        }

        string value = pattern.Trim().ToLowerInvariant();
        const string prefix = "https://";
        if (!value.StartsWith(prefix, StringComparison.Ordinal))
        {
            return false;
        }

        string host = value[prefix.Length..];
        if (host.Length == 0 || host.AsSpan().ContainsAny("/?#@ :"))
        {
            return false;
        }

        string bare = host.StartsWith("*.", StringComparison.Ordinal) ? host[2..] : host;
        return bare.Length > 0 && !bare.Contains('*') && bare.Contains('.');
    }
}
